The Gemini CLI application executes AI agents directly from the terminal. It allows these agents to understand and generate code, automate development workflows, and interact with local and external environments.

The application operates in both an interactive React-based UI and a non-interactive mode for scripting [Interactive UI and Non-Interactive Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-interactive-ui-and-non-interactive-execution). Its core framework manages configurations, commands, and prompts, including robust error handling and resource cleanup.

AI agent orchestration manages agent execution, delegates tasks to subagents, and handles communication with large language models (LLMs) [AI Agent Orchestration and Model Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management). Model availability checks and fallback mechanisms ensure resilient AI interactions [Model Availability and Fallback Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-model-availability-and-fallback-mechanisms). A policy engine enforces rules for agent actions, and a hook system provides extensive customization throughout the agent's lifecycle [Hook System for Agent Lifecycle Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-hook-system-for-agent-lifecycle-management).

Agents leverage a suite of built-in tools to perform actions:

- Interacting with the local file system and executing shell commands.
- Fetching web content and performing Google Search queries.
- Managing persistent memory across sessions and breaking down complex tasks.

An extensions framework allows for packaging custom tools, commands, and prompts. Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers further integrate external services and resources into the agent's capabilities [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-model-context-protocol-mcp-server-integration).

The CLI integrates with Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), such as VS Code, providing contextual awareness from the editor and enabling native diffing for proposed code changes [IDE Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ide-integration). An experimental Agent-to-Agent (A2A) server facilitates standardized client-agent communication, enabling real-time updates and tool execution [Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Communication Server](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#agent-to-agent-a2a-communication-server).

The application's operations can be executed within sandboxed environments using tools like Docker or Podman.

## Gemini CLI Application Core

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application provides terminal-based access to Gemini models, functioning as an AI agent for a variety of development tasks. It supports code understanding and generation, automates operational workflows, and integrates with external services. The application also offers advanced features such as grounding queries with Google Search for real-time information and conversational checkpointing. Authentication methods include [`Login with Google`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L133) (OAuth), [`Gemini API Key`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) for specific model control, and [`Vertex AI`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L177) for enterprise use cases, as outlined in [`README.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md).

The primary entry point for the CLI application is managed by files such as [`packages/cli/index.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/index.ts) and [`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx), which handle the initial setup, configuration loading, and argument parsing. This core orchestration logic allows for both interactive UI sessions, built with React using Ink, and non-interactive execution for programmatic use. This dual execution model is further detailed in [Interactive UI and Non-Interactive Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-interactive-ui-and-non-interactive-execution). Global error handling is a crucial aspect of the application's stability, distinguishing between expected and unexpected errors and ensuring proper resource cleanup during exit through mechanisms like [`runExitCleanup`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts#L47) from [`packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts). This robust approach to error management is elaborated in [Global Error Handling and Cleanup](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-global-error-handling-and-cleanup).

The architecture is designed for extensibility, integrating with [`MCP`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L320) (Model Context Protocol) servers for custom capabilities and leveraging a hook system to inject custom logic into an agent's execution lifecycle. The application's core functionalities, such as AI agent orchestration, LLM interaction, model availability, and policy enforcement, are managed within the [`packages/core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core) directory. The experimental Agent-to-Agent (A2A) server, located in [`packages/a2a-server`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server), further enhances client-agent communication by enabling real-time updates and tool execution.

The development workflow is supported by robust testing configurations, including unit tests with [`Vitest`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/GEMINI.md?plain=1#L34) and integration tests for various features, as described in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/CONTRIBUTING.md). The project's roadmap, outlined in [`ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/ROADMAP.md), emphasizes transparency and community involvement, with priorities managed via GitHub Issues.

### Application Entry Point and Initialization

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application's lifecycle begins with its main entry point, the [`main`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/lint.js#L339) function in [`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx). This function orchestrates the initial setup, configuration loading, argument parsing, and subsequent execution, leading to either an [Interactive UI and Non-Interactive Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-interactive-ui-and-non-interactive-execution) or a non-interactive command processing.

Upon launch, the application first handles command-line arguments using [`parseArguments`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/config.ts#L79) and merges them with application settings to construct a [`Config`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/config.ts#L329) object. This [`Config`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/config.ts#L329) object is crucial as it dictates various application behaviors, including how tools are excluded, the approval modes for operations, and which extensions are loaded. The application then performs an initial authentication step, potentially setting up necessary credentials. It also validates the DNS resolution order and UI theme settings to ensure a consistent and functional environment. If the CLI is running within an Integrated Development Environment (IDE), it establishes a connection with the IDE.

To prevent memory-related issues, especially during computationally intensive tasks, the application includes logic to determine if the Node.js process needs to be relaunched with increased memory allocation, adjusting the [`max-old-space-size`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L147) based on system resources. A global handler is also established to catch unhandled promise rejections, facilitating robust [Global Error Handling and Cleanup](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-global-error-handling-and-cleanup). Throughout this initialization phase, various cleanup functions are registered to ensure that resources are properly released when the application exits. Performance metrics are also collected during startup to monitor and optimize the application's launch time.

### Interactive UI and Non-Interactive Execution

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application operates in two distinct execution modes: an interactive, React-based terminal user interface and a non-interactive mode designed for programmatic use. This dual approach allows for rich, guided interactions as well as streamlined, scriptable command execution.

The primary entry point for the CLI, in [`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx), orchestrates the selection and management of these modes. Upon startup, after initial setup, configuration loading, and argument parsing, the application determines whether to launch the interactive UI or execute in non-interactive fashion.

The interactive UI is initiated through the [`startInteractiveUI`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L175) function within [`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx). This mode leverages [`ink`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/GEMINI.md?plain=1#L59), a React framework for building command-line interfaces, to render a dynamic and responsive user experience directly within the terminal. The UI manages various contexts such as settings, key presses, and mouse interactions, providing a rich environment for interacting with Gemini models. This includes features like real-time updates and an alternate screen buffer for a cleaner user experience. Within this mode, user input and commands are processed via custom React hooks, allowing for a highly interactive and responsive application.

Conversely, the non-interactive mode is engaged when the CLI is invoked for scriptable or single-shot commands, typically via [`--prompt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/index.md?plain=1#L54) arguments or standard input. In this mode, the [`runNonInteractive`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts#L56) function, defined in [`packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts), takes over. It processes user input programmatically, interacts with the AI, executes tools, and formats the output without rendering a persistent graphical interface. This mode is particularly suited for integration into scripts, automation workflows, or other applications where direct user interaction is not required. Before executing, non-interactive authentication is validated to ensure secure programmatic access.

Both execution modes utilize a shared foundation for configuration management, command loading, and prompt processing. The services located in [`packages/cli/src/services`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services) handle the loading and management of commands and prompts, irrespective of the execution mode. Global error handling mechanisms ensure that both interactive and non-interactive operations gracefully manage errors and perform necessary resource cleanup upon exit. For more details on the error handling mechanisms, refer to [Global Error Handling and Cleanup](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-global-error-handling-and-cleanup).

### Global Error Handling and Cleanup

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application incorporates mechanisms for handling errors and ensuring proper cleanup during its lifecycle. The main entry point, defined in [`packages/cli/index.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/index.ts), wraps the application's execution in a try-catch block to manage both anticipated and unexpected issues.

Expected errors, such as instances of [`FatalError`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/errors.ts#L28), are handled by displaying their specific message to the standard error stream and exiting with an associated error code. This allows for controlled termination when known, recoverable issues occur. For unexpected errors, a generic message is displayed, along with the error's stack trace if available, followed by an exit with a general error code. This distinction helps in debugging and providing appropriate user feedback.

Central to the application's stability is the [`runExitCleanup`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts#L47) function, defined in [`packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/utils/cleanup.ts). This function is invoked before the application exits, regardless of whether an error has occurred, to ensure that resources are properly released. This includes tasks such as closing open files, terminating background processes, or persisting transient data. The [`main`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/lint.js#L339) function in [`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx) also configures a [`setupUnhandledRejectionHandler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L153) to catch unhandled promise rejections, which are then logged and can trigger a debug console. This proactive approach to error management aims to prevent resource leaks and maintain data integrity during unexpected terminations.

### Configuration Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI manages its operational parameters through a robust configuration system that encompasses settings, authentication, extensions, policy enforcement, sandboxing, and keybindings. This system ensures consistent application behavior across different environments and user preferences.

Core application settings are loaded, merged, and validated from various scopes, including system defaults, user-specific configurations, and workspace-level overrides. This hierarchical loading ensures that preferences can be customized at different levels. The settings schema, defined in [`packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts), provides a structured definition for all configurable options, enabling schema-based validation to maintain data integrity. The system also handles the migration of deprecated settings, ensuring compatibility with older configurations. Environment variables can be resolved within configuration strings and objects, allowing for dynamic parameterization.

Authentication methods are validated to ensure that the CLI can securely interact with Gemini and other services. This validation checks for the presence of necessary environment variables or credentials depending on the chosen authentication type.

The CLI's extensibility is managed through a comprehensive framework for extensions. This includes loading, installing, updating, enabling, and disabling extensions, while also integrating security checks, workspace trust, and user consent. The system allows for custom tools and commands provided by extensions, and their configurations can include variables that are hydrated at runtime.

Policy enforcement is configured by translating application settings and approval modes into specific policies. This involves constructing [`PolicyEngineConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L184) objects that define how the CLI should evaluate function calls and other actions, often based on allow/deny lists and different approval behaviors. This ensures that the AI's actions align with user and organizational guidelines.

Sandboxing capabilities are integrated by dynamically loading sandbox configurations. This involves identifying available sandboxing commands (like Docker or Podman) and image URIs based on the current environment and settings, allowing the CLI to execute operations within isolated environments for security and consistency.

Keybindings are defined to provide a flexible system for keyboard shortcuts, allowing users to customize command execution through specific key combinations and modifiers. This system includes definitions for various commands and their categorization, enhancing user interaction with the CLI.

Finally, the CLI manages trusted folders, allowing users to define trust rules for specific directories. This mechanism helps determine if the current workspace is considered trusted, which can influence security-sensitive operations.

### Command and Prompt Services

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application manages and processes various types of commands and prompts, enabling interaction with AI agents and system functionalities. This includes built-in commands, commands loaded from files, and those sourced from Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The core logic for orchestrating command loading and execution resides within the [`packages/cli/src/services`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services) directory.

A central [`CommandService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/CommandService.ts#L22) within [`packages/cli/src/services`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services) coordinates the loading of commands from different sources. This service utilizes several implementations of [`ICommandLoader`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/types.ts#L17):

- [`BuiltinCommandLoader`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/BuiltinCommandLoader.ts#L50) handles the CLI's hard-coded slash commands, which provide fundamental functionalities.
- [`FileCommandLoader`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/FileCommandLoader.ts#L65) discovers and loads custom commands defined in TOML files, allowing users to extend the CLI's capabilities through local configurations.
- [`McpPromptLoader`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/McpPromptLoader.ts#L22) integrates prompts and commands provided by external MCP servers, expanding the range of available tools and interactions. For more details on MCP servers, see [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-model-context-protocol-mcp-server-integration).

Beyond command loading, the CLI also employs prompt processors, located in [`packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors), to dynamically transform user input before it is sent to an AI agent. These processors, which implement the [`IPromptProcessor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/types.ts#L20) interface, enable features like file content injection ( [`AtFileProcessor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/atFileProcessor.ts#L21)) and shell command execution ( [`ShellProcessor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/shellProcessor.ts#L54)). This modular approach to command and prompt management ensures flexibility and extensibility in how the CLI interacts with users and AI models.

### Zed Integration (Experimental)

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI includes an experimental integration for communication with graphical user interfaces (GUIs) like Zed via a JSON-RPC protocol known as the Agent Communication Protocol (ACP). This integration allows the CLI to act as a backend agent, receiving commands and sending updates to a GUI frontend.

The integration is managed within the experimental directory [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration). Communication is established through a [`Connection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/connection.ts#L92) ( [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration/connection.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/connection.ts)) that handles JSON-RPC messaging. The [`AgentSideConnection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/acp.ts#L16) ( [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration/acp.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/acp.ts)) further refines this by managing the ACP channel and defining the interfaces for interaction between the GUI client and the Gemini agent.

The core logic for initiating this integration resides in [`runZedIntegration`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L50) ( [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts)). This function is responsible for setting up the [`GeminiAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L66), which initializes the agent's capabilities, and a [`Session`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L218) object. The [`Session`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L218) handles chat sessions, processes prompts from the GUI, and manages the execution of tools on behalf of the agent.

To support operations requiring file system access, an [`AcpFileSystemService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/fileSystemService.ts#L13) ( [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration/fileSystemService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/fileSystemService.ts)) is provided. This service allows the agent to perform file system operations by delegating them to the connected GUI client or falling back to a local file system service if necessary. The structure of all ACP messages, ensuring type safety and consistency in communication, is defined using Zod schemas in [`packages/cli/src/zed-integration/schema.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/schema.ts).

## AI Agent Orchestration and Model Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI's core functionality for AI agent orchestration involves managing communication with the Gemini API, orchestrating tools, enforcing policies, handling session state, and performing context discovery to facilitate intelligent agent interactions. This is primarily handled within the [`packages/core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core) directory.

Central to this orchestration is the [`Config`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/config.ts#L329) class, defined in [`packages/core/src/config/config.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/config.ts), which acts as a central repository for application-wide settings and service initialization. It manages model configurations, tool registrations, feature toggles, and security settings, adapting behavior based on user settings and environmental factors. This configuration is crucial for how the CLI interfaces with large language models (LLMs) and other AI services.

Communication with LLMs is managed by the client components. For instance, the [`CodeAssistServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts#L64) in [`packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts) handles interactions with the Code Assist API for generative content requests, token counting, and user onboarding.
