### AI Agent Orchestration and Execution

link

zoom\_in

AI agents within the Gemini CLI are designed for modular and robust operation, particularly in agent-to-agent (A2A) contexts. The framework supports the definition, execution, and orchestration of these agents.

The [`AgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L81) in [`packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts) manages an agent's execution loop, overseeing interactions with generative models, tool calls, and chat history compression. It enforces termination conditions such as [`max_time_minutes`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L369) and [`max_turns`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L66), and attempts recovery from certain failures. Agents are expected to signal successful completion by calling a specific tool, and their output is validated against a defined schema. Security measures, like validating that only allowed tools are executed in non-interactive contexts, are also integrated.

Agent definitions are managed by the [`AgentRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts#L32) in [`packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts). This registry discovers, loads, and validates [`AgentDefinition`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L55) objects, providing mechanisms to retrieve agents and generate descriptions for tools and system prompts. It integrates with the application's configuration to apply model preferences and enable or disable agents, ensuring that model aliases are correctly registered for agent-specific models.

The system facilitates subagent invocation and delegation through the [`DelegateToAgentTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts#L26) in [`packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts) and [`SubagentInvocation`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts#L33) in [`packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts). The [`DelegateToAgentTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts#L26) enables a primary agent to invoke other registered subagents, dynamically generating a schema to validate delegation requests. [`SubagentInvocation`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts#L33) then orchestrates the actual subagent execution, streaming activities, and formatting results, while also handling comprehensive error management.

A specialized subagent for codebase analysis, the [`CodebaseInvestigatorAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts#L78) in [`packages/core/src/agents/codebase-investigator.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/codebase-investigator.ts), uses various tools to generate structured codebase investigation reports, including summaries of findings, exploration traces, and relevant code locations. To integrate subagents as tools, the [`SubagentToolWrapper`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts#L23) in [`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts) dynamically generates tool parameters from a subagent's input configuration, allowing subagents to function as standard declarative tools.

Foundational interfaces like [`AgentDefinition`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L55) define the configuration for prompts, models, runtime parameters, tools, outputs, and inputs. These interfaces are crucial for configuring and observing agent behavior. Additionally, utility functions for string templating, located in [`packages/core/src/agents/utils.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/utils.ts), are provided for populating placeholders in prompts and inputs, with error handling for missing keys.

The core logic for interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs) resides in [`packages/core/src/core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core). This includes managing API key storage, handling content generation requests ( [`generateJson`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts#L91), [`generateContent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts#L193), [`generateEmbedding`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts#L145)), and managing conversational interactions via [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68) and [`GeminiChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L210). These components handle session history, tool integration, and retry mechanisms. The [`HookSystem`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookSystem.ts#L21) provides a pluggable mechanism for injecting external logic into the agent's execution lifecycle, allowing for custom behaviors at various stages, as discussed in [Hook System for Agent Lifecycle Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-hook-system-for-agent-lifecycle-management). The [`CoreToolScheduler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L361) manages the entire lifecycle of tool calls, including validation, user confirmation, and execution. The [`Logger`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/logger.ts#L70) class handles persistent logging and checkpointing for saving and restoring agent state.

#### AI Agent Definition and Registration

link

zoom\_in

The definition, registration, and management of AI agents within the Gemini CLI are handled by a dedicated system that ensures agents can be discovered, loaded, and validated efficiently. This system is crucial for enabling modular and robust agent operations, especially in an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) context.

Central to this process is the concept of an [`AgentDefinition`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L55), which encapsulates the configuration necessary to describe an AI agent. These definitions include various aspects such as [`promptConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/prompts.ts#L138), [`modelConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts#L73), [`runConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L1055), [`toolConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L912), [`outputConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L737), and [`inputConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L65). These configurations collectively dictate how an agent interacts with the underlying Large Language Models (LLMs), what tools it can use, how it processes inputs, and what kind of output it is expected to produce.

The [`AgentRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts#L32) ( [`packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts)) is responsible for discovering, loading, and validating these [`AgentDefinition`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L55) objects. It integrates with the application's global configuration to apply model preferences and control which agents are enabled or disabled. This registry also plays a vital role in generating descriptions for tools and system prompts, which are then used by the LLMs to understand the available functionalities and their intended use. For instance, it ensures that model aliases specific to an agent are correctly registered and managed.

The design facilitates the integration of subagents as standard [`DeclarativeTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/tools.ts#L333) instances. The [`SubagentToolWrapper`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts#L23) ( [`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts)) dynamically generates tool parameters from a subagent's [`inputConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/types.ts#L65), effectively allowing subagents to be treated and invoked like any other tool. This mechanism is supported by utility functions that convert input configurations into JSON schemas ( [`packages/core/src/agents/schema-utils.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/schema-utils.ts)), enabling dynamic validation of subagent delegation requests.

This structured approach to agent definition and registration is fundamental for the broader AI agent orchestration within the Gemini CLI, allowing for flexible agent development and consistent execution across the platform. More information on how these agents are executed and orchestrated can be found in [AI Agent Orchestration and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-ai-agent-orchestration-and-execution).

#### Subagent Delegation and Invocation

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI supports the delegation of tasks to subagents, enabling a hierarchical approach to complex problem-solving. This mechanism allows a primary agent to break down a large task into smaller, more specialized subtasks and assign them to other agents that possess specific capabilities.

The core of subagent delegation is facilitated by the [`DelegateToAgentTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts#L26) found in [`packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/delegate-to-agent-tool.ts). This tool empowers an agent to invoke other registered subagents within the system. To ensure valid delegation requests, it dynamically generates a schema based on the available subagents in the [`AgentRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/registry.ts#L32), which is responsible for discovering, loading, and validating agent definitions (see [AI Agent Definition and Registration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-ai-agent-orchestration-and-execution-ai-agent-definition-and-registration)).

Once a delegation request is validated, the [`SubagentInvocation`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts#L33) in [`packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/invocation.ts) orchestrates the actual execution of the subagent. It manages the subagent's execution lifecycle via the [`AgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/executor.ts#L81) (see [AI Agent Orchestration and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-ai-agent-orchestration-and-execution)), streams intermediate activities, and formats the subagent's results for the calling agent.

To allow subagents to be treated as standard tools, the [`SubagentToolWrapper`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts#L23) in [`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts) dynamically generates tool parameters from a subagent's input configuration. This abstraction ensures that subagents can seamlessly integrate into the tool ecosystem, making their functionalities accessible and manageable.

### Model Availability and Fallback Mechanisms

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI manages model health, implements fallback strategies based on defined policies, and classifies errors to ensure resilient AI interactions even when models encounter issues. This system is crucial for maintaining continuous operation and providing a consistent user experience despite potential API outages, quota limits, or model performance variations.

The core of this system is responsible for tracking the operational status of different AI models. It can mark models as healthy, terminally unavailable (due to persistent issues like quota exhaustion or capacity limits), or temporarily unavailable with a "retry once per turn" mechanism for transient failures. This allows the system to make informed decisions about which models to use.

A key aspect of ensuring resilience is the implementation of policy-driven fallback mechanisms. When a model encounters an error during content generation, the system classifies the nature of the failure (e.g., terminal, transient, not found). Based on this classification and predefined policies, it determines appropriate actions. These policies, which can be configured and dynamically updated, define how the system should react to different failure types, including options like automatically retrying the request with another available model, prompting the user for an action, or initiating an upgrade process.

For a deeper understanding of how these policies are structured and evaluated, see [Policy Configuration and Evaluation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-policy-enforcement-and-confirmation-bus-policy-configuration-and-evaluation). The system can dynamically choose between different fallback strategies, including a legacy approach for specific scenarios or a more advanced policy-driven approach that leverages a service to intelligently select fallback candidates. User intent is also integrated into this process, allowing the system to process user choices such as retrying the request immediately, stopping the operation, or upgrading their service. This dynamic approach ensures that the CLI can adapt to various error conditions and maintain robust AI interactions.

#### Model Health Tracking and Selection

link

zoom\_in

The [`ModelAvailabilityService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts#L41) in [`packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts) plays a central role in managing the operational status of different AI models. It tracks the health of models by marking them as either healthy or unhealthy, and it implements strategies for handling transient and terminal failures.

This service utilizes a [`HealthState`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts#L19) mechanism to record a model's current status, which can indicate if a model is unavailable due to issues like quota limits or capacity shortages. It provides functions to explicitly mark a model as terminally unavailable, signaling persistent issues, or as healthy when it recovers. For temporary interruptions, a "retry once per turn" mechanism allows for a single retry attempt within a given conversational turn, with state resets for subsequent turns.

A key function of the [`ModelAvailabilityService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts#L41) is to select an available model from a given list, considering their current health status and any defined retry policies. This ensures that the system attempts to use a functional model, skipping those that are currently experiencing issues. The process also logs any models that were skipped and the reasons for their unavailability. The service's ability to classify failures (as detailed in [Model Availability and Fallback Mechanisms](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-model-availability-and-fallback-mechanisms)) into categories like [`'terminal'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts#L197), [`'transient'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L21), or [`'not_found'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts#L197) is crucial for making informed decisions about model selection and fallback strategies.

#### Policy-Driven Fallback Strategies

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI employs policy-driven fallback mechanisms to ensure resilient AI interactions, particularly when models encounter issues. This system is designed to intelligently handle errors by categorizing them, applying predefined policies, and presenting users with options for recovery, such as retrying with a different model or upgrading their service.

The core of this system is the [`ModelAvailabilityService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts#L41) in [`packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts), which tracks the health of various models. When a model fails, the system classifies the error into a [`FailureKind`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L21) (e.g., [`'terminal'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts#L197), [`'transient'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L21)) using [`classifyFailureKind`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/errorClassification.ts#L14) in [`packages/core/src/availability/errorClassification.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/errorClassification.ts). This classification is crucial for determining the appropriate fallback action.

[`ModelPolicy`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L44) objects, potentially defined in TOML files and managed by [`packages/core/src/availability/policyCatalog.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/policyCatalog.ts), dictate how the system should react to different [`FailureKind`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L21) s for specific models. These policies are organized into [`ModelPolicyChain`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L55) s, which provide an ordered sequence of fallback options. For instance, a policy might specify that a [`'transient'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L21) error should trigger a retry with a different model, while a [`'terminal'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts#L197) error might suggest a more drastic action, like offering an upgrade.

The [`handleFallback`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/handler.ts#L31) function in [`packages/core/src/fallback/handler.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/handler.ts) orchestrates this process. When a model failure occurs, it uses the [`ModelAvailabilityService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelAvailabilityService.ts#L41) and the [`ModelPolicyChain`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/availability/modelPolicy.ts#L55) to identify suitable fallback candidates. The system then processes [`FallbackIntent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/types.ts#L17) from the user, which can include choices like [`'retry_always'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/types.ts#L18), [`'retry_once'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/types.ts#L19), [`'stop'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L360), or [`'upgrade'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/fallback/types.ts#L22). This user intent guides the system in taking actions such as switching the active model, activating a fallback mode, or directing the user to an upgrade page.

This policy-driven approach allows for flexible and configurable error handling, enabling the CLI to adapt to various model availability scenarios and provide a more robust and user-friendly experience. See also [Model Health Tracking and Selection](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-model-availability-and-fallback-mechanisms-model-health-tracking-and-selection) for more information on how models are tracked. The [LLM Client and Chat Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-llm-client-and-chat-management) section provides more context on overall LLM interaction.

### LLM Client and Chat Management

link

zoom\_in

The [`packages/core/src/core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core) directory contains the foundational logic for interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs). This includes managing API keys, generating content, handling conversational sessions, and implementing robust retry mechanisms.

API key management is handled by utilities that load, save, and clear API keys from secure storage, ensuring that credentials are managed persistently and safely. This process often leverages a [`HybridTokenStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/token-storage/hybrid-token-storage.ts#L14) mechanism, which can prioritize system keychains for enhanced security. For further detail on credential management, refer to [API Key and Credential Storage](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-llm-client-and-chat-management-api-key-and-credential-storage).

Content generation from LLMs is managed through an interface that supports various generation types, including structured JSON output, general text content, and numerical embeddings. This system incorporates retry logic with backoff strategies and dynamic model selection to ensure resilient content delivery, even when models encounter transient issues. The choice of content generator depends on the authentication type and specific configuration, allowing for flexibility in how interactions are handled, from fake generators for testing to robust clients for production environments.

Conversational interactions are orchestrated by classes such as [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68) and [`GeminiChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L210). These components manage the lifecycle of chat sessions, including initialization, starting new chats, resetting conversations, and resuming from previous states. They are responsible for sending user messages and receiving streamed responses from the LLM. Key functionalities include the integration of various hooks that allow external logic to intercept and modify the agent's behavior at different stages of the conversation. The chat management system also addresses practical challenges such as context window overflow by implementing chat compression techniques and handles robust retry mechanisms for invalid content or network errors. For a deeper understanding of conversation management, see [Conversational Interaction Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-llm-client-and-chat-management-conversational-interaction-management).

The system also includes a [`CoreToolScheduler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L361) that manages the execution of tools during agent interactions. This scheduler handles the queuing and processing of tool calls, including validation, user confirmation, and execution. It can automatically approve certain tool calls based on predefined [`ApprovalMode`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L45) settings and manages the truncation of large tool outputs for display, while saving the full content to temporary files for later reference.

#### API Key and Credential Storage

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI manages API keys and OAuth credentials through a robust storage system primarily found within the [`packages/core/src/mcp`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp) directory. This system is designed for secure and persistent storage, supporting various authentication methods including Google Application Default Credentials (ADC), OAuth 2.0 with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), and service account impersonation.

API keys, such as those used for direct access to Large Language Models, are handled by the functions in [`packages/core/src/core/apiKeyCredentialStorage.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/apiKeyCredentialStorage.ts). These functions allow for loading, saving, and clearing API keys, utilizing a [`HybridTokenStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/token-storage/hybrid-token-storage.ts#L14) mechanism for secure and persistent storage. The API key is internally wrapped in an [`OAuthCredentials`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/token-storage/types.ts#L21) format with a [`tokenType: 'ApiKey'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/apiKeyCredentialStorage.ts#L56) for consistent handling across the system.

For OAuth credentials, the [`MCPOAuthTokenStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-token-storage.ts#L26) in [`packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-token-storage.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-token-storage.ts) provides persistence. This storage mechanism offers dual modes: a default JSON file storage and an encrypted hybrid storage option. The hybrid approach prioritizes the use of system-native keychains via [`KeychainTokenStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/token-storage/hybrid-token-storage.ts#L28) for enhanced security. If a keychain is unavailable or explicitly overridden, it gracefully falls back to [`FileTokenStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/token-storage/file-token-storage.ts#L15), which encrypts credentials within a JSON file using AES-256-GCM encryption with a system-specific key. This layered approach ensures credentials are managed securely, adapting to the environment's capabilities.

Authentication providers, such as [`GoogleCredentialProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/google-auth-provider.ts#L21) (for ADC), [`MCPOAuthProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-provider.ts#L99) (for OAuth 2.0), and [`ServiceAccountImpersonationProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/mcp/sa-impersonation-provider.ts#L25), manage the acquisition and refreshing of access tokens, handling caching and host validation to prevent credential leakage. Further details on these providers can be found in [LLM Client and Chat Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-llm-client-and-chat-management).

#### Conversational Interaction Management

link

zoom\_in

Conversational interactions with Large Language Models (LLMs) are managed primarily through the [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68) and [`GeminiChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L210) classes. These components handle the lifecycle of chat sessions, from initiation to termination, and orchestrate message streaming, conversational history management, and the integration of various tools.

The [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68) ( [`packages/core/src/core/client.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts)) serves as the central orchestrator for chat sessions. It provides methods to initialize, start, reset, and resume conversations. A core function within [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68) is [`sendMessageStream`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L261), which facilitates sending user requests and receiving streamed responses from the LLM. This method integrates with various hooks (e.g., [`fireBeforeAgentHook`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/clientHookTriggers.ts#L31), [`fireAfterAgentHook`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/clientHookTriggers.ts#L74)) for pre- and post-processing of agent responses, manages the flow of turns in a conversation, and dynamically adjusts for context window overflows by attempting chat compression ( [`tryCompressChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L487)). It can also inject relevant IDE context from the development environment and detect potential conversational loops using a [`LoopDetectionService`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/services/loopDetectionService.ts#L100).

The [`GeminiChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L210) class ( [`packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts)) specifically manages the details of a single chat session. Its [`sendMessageStream`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L261) method is responsible for the actual message streaming, maintaining the conversational history, integrating tools for dynamic interactions, and providing robust retry mechanisms to handle issues such as invalid content or network errors ( [`InvalidStreamError`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L187)). It can dynamically adjust parameters like [`temperature`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts#L31) during retries and manages fallback strategies, such as switching to preview models when necessary. [`GeminiChat`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts#L210) also provides functionalities for managing the conversational history, allowing retrieval, addition, and modification of messages, and distinguishing between curated and comprehensive historical records.

The system incorporates a comprehensive hook system that allows external logic to intercept and modify the agent's behavior throughout the conversational process. Hooks like [`fireBeforeModelHook`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChatHookTriggers.ts#L71), [`fireBeforeToolSelectionHook`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChatHookTriggers.ts#L139), and [`fireAfterModelHook`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/geminiChatHookTriggers.ts#L194) enable the modification of LLM requests, tool configurations, or response chunks, ensuring flexibility and extensibility in how the agent processes information and interacts with users. Further details on this system can be found in [Hook System for Agent Lifecycle Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-hook-system-for-agent-lifecycle-management).

Tool execution within conversations is managed by the [`CoreToolScheduler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L361) ( [`packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts)), which handles the scheduling and lifecycle of tool calls, including validation, user confirmation, and execution. It can determine if a tool call can be automatically approved based on predefined [`ApprovalMode`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L45) settings. This scheduler also manages the logging of tool outputs and can truncate large outputs for display while saving full content to temporary files. See [Built-in Tools for Local Environment Interaction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-built-in-tools-for-local-environment-interaction) for more information on the tools themselves.

For persistence, the [`Logger`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/logger.ts#L70) class ( [`packages/core/src/core/logger.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/logger.ts)) handles logging to [`logs.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/logger.ts#L15) and provides checkpointing capabilities. It allows for saving, loading, and deleting conversation checkpoints, which are identified by unique tags, enabling the restoration of previous conversational states. This is crucial for maintaining context across sessions and recovering from interruptions.

### Policy Enforcement and Confirmation Bus

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI employs a robust system for policy configuration, enforcement, and persistence, alongside an inter-agent communication bus for managing tool confirmations and hook requests. This system is primarily managed within the [`packages/core/src/policy`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy) and [`packages/core/src/confirmation-bus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus) directories.

The core of this system is the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93), which evaluates requests for tool executions ( [`FunctionCall`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L7) objects) and hook executions against a set of predefined and dynamically loaded policies. These policies, defined as [`PolicyRule`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L97) s, [`SafetyCheckerRule`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L122) s, and [`HookCheckerRule`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L158) s, determine whether an action should be [`ALLOW`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L10) ed, [`DENY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L11) ed, or require [`ASK_USER`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L12) confirmation. Policies are loaded from TOML files, aggregated from various sources (default, user, administrative), and assigned priorities to ensure correct precedence. For instance, command-line flags or MCP server configurations can dynamically inject rules with specific priorities. The [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93) also includes specialized logic for shell command safety, parsing and recursively checking sub-commands to aggregate the most restrictive decision.

Supporting this enforcement is the [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18), located within the [`packages/core/src/confirmation-bus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus) directory. This bus facilitates inter-agent communication, specifically for [`TOOL_CONFIRMATION_REQUEST`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L10) and [`HOOK_EXECUTION_REQUEST`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L16) messages. When such messages are published, the [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) consults the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93) to obtain a [`PolicyDecision`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L9). For tool confirmation requests, the [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) handles the interactive [`ASK_USER`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L12) scenario, awaiting user input. However, for hook execution requests, any decision other than [`ALLOW`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L10) results in an immediate denial, as hooks do not support interactive confirmation. The [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) also supports dynamically updating policies in response to [`UPDATE_POLICY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L15) messages, allowing for user-defined rules (e.g., from interactive UI selections) to be persisted to an [`auto-saved.toml`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts#L286) file.

To ensure consistency in security policy matching, particularly for [`argsPattern`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L108) regular expressions, the system uses a [`stableStringify`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/stable-stringify.ts#L59) function. This function produces a deterministic JSON string representation with sorted keys, handling complexities like circular references to maintain predictable policy evaluations.

#### Policy Configuration and Evaluation

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI employs a robust policy engine to manage and enforce rules governing function calls and hook executions. This system ensures that agents operate within defined boundaries, providing a layer of security and controlled behavior.

Policies are loaded from TOML files, enabling administrators and users to define rules that specify whether certain actions are allowed, denied, or require user confirmation. The system aggregates policies from default configurations, user-defined settings, and administrative overrides, establishing a tiered priority system to resolve conflicts. For example, [`settings.mcp.excluded`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts#L169) tools receive a high priority to ensure security-critical blocks, while [`settings.tools.allowed`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts#L196) tools also have a defined priority. This dynamic configuration allows for flexible adjustments based on application settings, MCP server configurations, and specific tool allowances or exclusions. This aggregation process is managed by [`createPolicyEngineConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/policy.ts#L18) in [`packages/core/src/policy/config.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts).

The [`loadPoliciesFromToml`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts#L227) function, found in [`packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts), handles parsing these TOML files and validating their contents against predefined schemas. During this process, it transforms rules by expanding fields like [`commandPrefix`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/persistence.test.ts#L108) and [`commandRegex`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/core/policy-engine.md?plain=1#L172) into regular expressions for more flexible matching, and combines [`mcpName`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/persistence.test.ts#L146) with [`toolName`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L749) to create [`effectiveToolName`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/toml-loader.ts#L367) for clearer rule application.

The central component for policy enforcement is the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93), defined in [`packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts). This engine evaluates [`FunctionCall`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L7) objects and hook execution requests against configured [`PolicyRule`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L97) s and [`SafetyCheckerRule`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L122) s. It produces a [`PolicyDecision`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L9)—either [`ALLOW`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L10), [`DENY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L11), or [`ASK_USER`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L12)—based on the most restrictive rule that applies. Rules are evaluated in descending order of priority, ensuring that more specific or critical policies take precedence. The engine includes specialized logic for handling shell commands, recursively checking sub-commands to aggregate the most restrictive policy decision. In non-interactive modes, any [`ASK_USER`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L12) decision automatically becomes [`DENY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L11) to prevent the application from hanging. Furthermore, user-defined policies can be dynamically added to the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93) through the [`createPolicyUpdater`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/policy.ts#L33) in [`packages/core/src/policy/config.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts), especially when an interactive UI decision (like "Always Allow") needs to be persisted. These new rules are saved to an [`auto-saved.toml`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/config.ts#L286) file, using atomic write operations to prevent data corruption.

For consistent policy matching, especially with regular expressions, the [`stableStringify`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/stable-stringify.ts#L59) function in [`packages/core/src/policy/stable-stringify.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/stable-stringify.ts) provides a deterministic JSON string representation with sorted keys. This ensures that the evaluation of policy rules against complex arguments remains consistent across different executions. The policy engine also integrates with a [`CheckerRunner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/safety/checker-runner.ts#L55) to perform additional safety checks beyond the basic rule matching, further enhancing the security posture of the agent's operations. The policy enforcement system works closely with the [Inter-Agent Communication and Confirmation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-policy-enforcement-and-confirmation-bus-inter-agent-communication-and-confirmation) system to facilitate confirmations.

#### Inter-Agent Communication and Confirmation

zoom\_in

The [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) facilitates communication between various components within the Gemini CLI, particularly for scenarios requiring tool confirmation and hook execution. This publish-subscribe mechanism, implemented in [`packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts), enables components to send and receive messages, ensuring type-safe handling through predefined message structures in [`packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts).

A critical aspect of the [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) is its integration with the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93). For messages requesting tool confirmation ( [`TOOL_CONFIRMATION_REQUEST`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L10)) or hook execution ( [`HOOK_EXECUTION_REQUEST`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L16)), the [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) consults the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93) to determine the appropriate action: [`ALLOW`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L10), [`DENY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L11), or [`ASK_USER`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L12). This ensures that actions are aligned with established policies before proceeding. For instance, if the [`PolicyEngine`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L93)'s decision is anything other than [`ALLOW`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/types.ts#L10) for a [`HOOK_EXECUTION_REQUEST`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/types.ts#L16), the hook is immediately denied, as hooks do not support interactive user confirmation. The [`MessageBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/confirmation-bus/message-bus.ts#L18) also supports a request-response pattern, allowing for more synchronous-like interactions over the asynchronous bus. This involves sending a message and awaiting a correlated response, leveraging unique identifiers and timeouts to manage the interaction. For a broader understanding of policy enforcement, refer to [Policy Enforcement and Confirmation Bus](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-policy-enforcement-and-confirmation-bus).

### Hook System for Agent Lifecycle Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI incorporates a pluggable hook system that allows custom logic to be injected into an agent's execution lifecycle. This system provides a way to observe, modify, and enhance the behavior of AI agents without altering their core source code. It supports various customization scenarios, from policy enforcement to dynamic context injection.

The [`HookSystem`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookSystem.ts#L21) class, located in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookSystem.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookSystem.ts), orchestrates this functionality. It coordinates the registration, planning, execution, and aggregation of hooks. Hooks are defined and managed by the [`HookRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts#L37) in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts), which loads and validates hook definitions from various configuration sources (e.g., project-specific settings, user preferences, or extensions) and prioritizes them based on their origin.

Before hooks are executed, the [`HookPlanner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L15), defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts), generates an execution plan. This plan determines which hooks are relevant for a given event and whether they should run sequentially or in parallel. The system allows for flexible matching criteria, such as exact string matches, regular expressions, or wildcards, to target hooks to specific contexts or tool invocations.

The actual execution of command-line hooks is handled by the [`HookRunner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts#L36) in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts). This component manages the spawning of child processes, handles their standard input/output, enforces timeouts, and interprets the results. Hooks communicate with the system using JSON-formatted input via [`stdin`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L57) and output via [`stdout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L1064), allowing for structured data exchange.

After execution, the results from multiple hooks are combined by the [`HookAggregator`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts#L36), which is defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts). This component applies event-specific merging logic to consolidate the outputs into a single aggregated result. For instance, in tool-related events, it can prioritize blocking decisions or combine fields, while for model-related events, later hook outputs might override earlier ones.

The [`HookEventHandler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookEventHandler.ts#L277) in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookEventHandler.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookEventHandler.ts) manages the lifecycle of different hook events, such as [`SessionStart`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1527), [`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491), [`AfterModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1575), [`BeforeToolSelection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1587), and [`AfterTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1479). It coordinates the planning, running, and aggregation processes for these events, and also handles asynchronous hook execution requests received via the [Inter-Agent Communication and Confirmation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-policy-enforcement-and-confirmation-bus-inter-agent-communication-and-confirmation) message bus.

A crucial aspect of the hook system is its ability to translate between the internal LLM request/response formats and the external SDK formats. This is facilitated by the [`HookTranslator`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookTranslator.ts#L75), defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookTranslator.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookTranslator.ts). This translation ensures compatibility and provides a simplified, text-focused interface for hooks, filtering non-text content to streamline interaction.

Together, these components provide a robust and flexible framework for extending and customizing agent behavior throughout its execution lifecycle. For more information on how hooks are configured and developed, refer to [Customizing Agent Behavior with Hooks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-customizing-agent-behavior-with-hooks).

#### Hook Registration and Planning

link

zoom\_in

The hook system allows for the injection of custom logic at various points in an AI agent's execution lifecycle. This is managed through a process of registration, validation, and planning.

Hook definitions are managed by the [`HookRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts#L37) class, primarily defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts). This component is responsible for loading and processing hook configurations from different sources, such as project-specific settings, user configurations, and extensions. Hooks are prioritized based on their origin, allowing for consistent and predictable behavior when multiple hooks might apply to the same event. The [`HookRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.ts#L37) also validates that hook definitions conform to expected schemas, logging warnings for any invalid entries to help maintain system integrity. It enables the dynamic enabling or disabling of hooks, providing flexibility in controlling their execution.

Once hooks are registered, the [`HookPlanner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L15) (defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts)) takes over to generate an execution plan. For each [`HookEventName`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L23), the [`HookPlanner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L15) determines which registered hooks are relevant based on their [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) properties, which can specify exact strings, regular expressions, or wildcards to match various criteria (e.g., specific tool names or triggers). The [`HookPlanner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L15) also dictates whether these hooks should execute sequentially or in parallel, optimizing for either dependency chain enforcement or performance. This planning phase ensures that only applicable hooks are considered and executed in the correct order for a given event, ultimately forming a [`HookExecutionPlan`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L597).

#### Hook Execution and Aggregation

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI's hook system provides mechanisms for executing and aggregating the results of command-line hooks. The [`HookRunner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts#L36) component, defined in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts), is responsible for executing these external command-line hooks. It manages the entire process from spawning child processes to handling standard input/output ( [`stdin`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L57)/ [`stdout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L1064)/ [`stderr`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L1065)) and enforcing timeouts. Hooks receive [`HookInput`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L78) in JSON format via [`stdin`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/zedIntegration.ts#L57) and are expected to return [`HookOutput`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L89) as JSON via [`stdout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L1064). The [`HookRunner`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts#L36) also interprets the command's exit code and output to determine the hook's decision, such as [`'allow'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md?plain=1#L675) or [`'deny'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md?plain=1#L665), and handles environment variable expansion within hook commands. Hooks can be executed either sequentially or in parallel, depending on the [`HookExecutionPlan`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L597) generated by the [Hook Registration and Planning](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-hook-system-for-agent-lifecycle-management-hook-registration-and-planning) process. In sequential execution, the output of one hook can be applied as input to the next, allowing for chained transformations.

After execution, the [`HookAggregator`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts#L36) component, located in [`packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts), combines the results from multiple hook executions into a single, cohesive [`AggregatedHookResult`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts#L25). This aggregation process applies event-specific merging logic. For events such as [`BeforeTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1467), [`AfterTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1479), [`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491), [`AfterAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1503), and [`SessionStart`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1527), the aggregator prioritizes blocking decisions ( [`'block'`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L69)) and [`continue: false`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookAggregator.ts#L118) flags, effectively short-circuiting further actions if a hook dictates. For [`BeforeModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1563) and [`AfterModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1575) events, later [`hookSpecificOutput`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/types.ts#L96) values overwrite earlier ones, allowing hooks to refine or replace previous outputs. When aggregating results for [`BeforeToolSelection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1587), it produces a union of [`allowedFunctionNames`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookTranslator.ts#L69), with [`NONE`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/editor.ts#L159) mode taking precedence over [`ANY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/LICENSE#L147) and [`AUTO`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L215), thus influencing which tools can be selected by the agent. This ensures that the collective decisions and modifications made by all relevant hooks are coherently applied to the agent's workflow.

#### OAuth2 Authentication and User Management

zoom\_in

OAuth2 authentication for Code Assist manages secure user access and token handling within the Gemini CLI. This process supports various authentication flows, including web-based methods for user interaction, user-code flows, and Compute Engine Application Default Credentials (ADC) for cloud environments. The system ensures secure storage and efficient retrieval of authentication tokens.

Core to this is the management of OAuth2 tokens, which involves caching to minimize repetitive authentication requests and refreshing expired tokens to maintain continuous access. Credentials are securely stored, prioritizing system keychains for enhanced security and falling back to file-based storage when necessary. This robust storage mechanism is handled by [`OAuthCredentialStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth-credential-storage.ts#L20) in [`packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth-credential-storage.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth-credential-storage.ts), which also includes a migration path from older storage methods.

User setup for Code Assist, orchestrated by [`packages/core/src/code_assist/setup.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/setup.ts), involves determining the appropriate Google Cloud Project ID and the user's service tier. The system also handles client-side experiment management, allowing for dynamic feature flags and configurations. OAuth client management and token operations are primarily handled by the functions within [`packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts). These functions facilitate obtaining authenticated clients, managing specific login flows, and clearing cached credentials when required.

Core CLI commands are managed within the system to handle tasks such as listing available extensions, initializing new projects, and restoring an agent's previous state. If this file does not exist, the system triggers an AI agent to analyze the current directory and generate appropriate content for [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113), thereby automating the setup process.

This functionality leverages an asynchronous generator to stream updates during the restoration process, providing feedback to the user.

A critical aspect of command processing is the use of standardized return types, defined in [`packages/core/src/commands/types.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts). These types dictate how command actions communicate their outcomes, enabling diverse responses such as scheduling a tool call ( [`ToolActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L11)), displaying a message to the user ( [`MessageActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L21)), replacing the conversation history ( [`LoadHistoryActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L31)), or submitting a prompt to a Gemini model ( [`SubmitPromptActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L41)).
