Project initialization is facilitated by the [`performInit`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/init.ts#L9) function, defined in [`packages/core/src/commands/init.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/init.ts). This function aims to ensure the presence of a [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) file, which serves as a project descriptor for the AI agent. If [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) is not found in the project directory, [`performInit`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/init.ts#L9) does not create it directly. Instead, it issues a [`submit_prompt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/types.ts#L378) command, which contains a detailed, structured prompt. This prompt instructs an AI agent to analyze the current directory's contents, determine the project's nature (e.g., code repository, documentation project), and then generate appropriate content for [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113). This approach delegates the intelligent generation of project documentation to the AI, adapting it to the specific context of the project. If [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) already exists, [`performInit`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/init.ts#L9) simply indicates that no changes are needed.

Conversely, the [`performRestore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/restore.ts#L11) function, an asynchronous generator located in [`packages/core/src/commands/restore.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/restore.ts), is responsible for reconstructing an agent's operational state from a checkpoint. This includes restoring conversational history and, if specified, reverting the project's file system to a particular Git revision. When provided with [`history`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L202) and [`clientHistory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/checkpointUtils.ts#L128) data, [`performRestore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/restore.ts#L11) issues a [`load_history`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L32) command to update the agent's conversational context. If a [`commitHash`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/checkpointUtils.ts#L136) is present in the [`toolCallData`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/checkpointUtils.ts#L170), the function interacts with a Git service to revert the project's files to that specific commit. The use of an asynchronous generator allows for streaming updates during the restoration process, providing feedback on progress or any encountered errors, such as issues with Git operations. The different actions that can be returned by these commands, such as [`ToolActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L11), [`MessageActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L21), [`LoadHistoryActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L31), and [`SubmitPromptActionReturn`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts#L41), are standardized to ensure consistent communication and processing within the CLI. These types are defined in [`packages/core/src/commands/types.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/types.ts).

## Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Communication Server

link

zoom\_in

The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) server is an experimental component of the Gemini CLI, designed to standardize client-agent communication. Its role is to bridge the Gemini CLI agent with external clients, such as Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), enabling real-time updates and facilitating the execution of agent-driven tools. This server manages the entire lifecycle of agent tasks, processes command-line interface (CLI) commands, handles configuration, and provides an HTTP API for seamless interactions.

The server's core functionality is implemented within the [`packages/a2a-server`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server) directory. It defines a [`development-tool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/development-extension-rfc.md?plain=1#L1) extension, crucial for standardizing how clients interact with the Gemini CLI agent. This extension uses structured schema definitions, such as [`AgentSettings`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/types.ts#L46), [`ToolCall`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L20), [`ConfirmationRequest`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/types.ts#L404), and [`AgentThought`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/development-extension-rfc.md?plain=1#L287), to allow for detailed communication regarding the agent's state, actions, and internal reasoning.

Central to the A2A server is its agent task management system, which orchestrates the full lifecycle of tasks, particularly for code generation. This includes creating new tasks, managing their execution, handling their internal state transitions, and persisting their progress. This system also facilitates communication with the Gemini Large Language Model (LLM) and manages the scheduling and execution of various tools. Further details on how AI agents are orchestrated and managed can be found in [AI Agent Orchestration and Model Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management).

The A2A server integrates CLI commands directly into its operational model. This allows external clients to trigger and manage operations like listing installed extensions, initializing new projects, or restoring previous agent states from checkpoints. These commands are executed by the agent executor, with results and updates streamed back to the client. For an in-depth understanding of how the core CLI commands function, refer to [Command Processing and State Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-command-processing-and-state-management).

Configuration management within the A2A server is robust, handling application settings, environment variables, and the discovery and loading of Gemini CLI extensions. This ensures that the agent operates within a well-defined and customizable environment, adapting to specific project requirements and user preferences. The comprehensive approach to configuration is further elaborated in [Configuration Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-configuration-management).

Finally, the A2A server exposes an HTTP API to facilitate interactions with clients. This API enables tasks such as creating new agent tasks, executing CLI commands with streaming updates, retrieving lists of available commands, and accessing task-specific metadata. This HTTP interface uses streaming interactions to provide real-time feedback to clients, ensuring a dynamic and responsive user experience. The management of communication with external systems, including JSON-RPC and MCP servers, is discussed in [Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-model-context-protocol-mcp-server-integration) and [Zed Integration (Experimental)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core-zed-integration-experimental).

### Agent Task Lifecycle and Execution

link

zoom\_in

The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) server within the Gemini CLI manages the lifecycle and execution of agent tasks, particularly for code generation. This system orchestrates agent interactions, handles tool execution, and manages state persistence for ongoing conversations and operations.

The central component for managing agent tasks is the [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83) located in [`packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts). This executor is responsible for creating new tasks, retrieving existing ones, and reconstructing tasks from previously persisted states. Its primary function is to drive the agent's interaction loop, which involves processing user messages, managing tool calls, and handling responses from the Gemini Large Language Model (LLM).

Each individual agent task is encapsulated by the [`Task`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L62) class in [`packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts). This class maintains the task's current state (e.g., 'submitted', 'input-required', 'working', 'canceled', 'failed', 'completed') and facilitates communication with the LLM through a [`GeminiClient`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L68). The [`Task`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L62) class also integrates with a [`CoreToolScheduler`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L361) to manage the execution of various tools. This includes dispatching tool calls, waiting for their completion, and feeding the results back to the LLM for further processing.

A key aspect of task execution is the tool confirmation flow. When a tool requires user approval, the [`Task`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L62) class manages [`pendingToolConfirmationDetails`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L68) and handles user responses, which can include options like [`ProceedOnce`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/tools.ts#L721) or [`Cancel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L575). The system also supports automatic approval in certain configurations (e.g., [`ApprovalMode.YOLO`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts#L110)). For tasks involving file modifications, such as those that edit code, the system creates checkpoints and applies proposed replacements to the workspace.

The [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83) also manages task cancellation. This involves updating the task's state to 'canceled', persisting this change, and publishing relevant events. [`AbortController`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L522) and [`abortSignal`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/core/client.ts#L736) mechanisms are used to propagate cancellation requests through the asynchronous execution flow, allowing for the graceful termination of operations. Furthermore, the system detects client disconnections and can automatically trigger task cancellation in such scenarios.

Configuration for each task is loaded dynamically by the [`getConfig`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L90) method of [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83). This process involves setting the target directory, loading environment variables, applying settings, and integrating agent extensions. This dynamic loading ensures that each task operates with the appropriate tools and functionalities.

Task state and agent settings are persisted using a [`TaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L10) (e.g., [`GCSTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L33) described in [Task Persistence with Google Cloud Storage](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#agent-to-agent-a2a-communication-server-task-persistence-with-google-cloud-storage)). The [`TaskWrapper`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L44) class provides an abstraction layer that enables serialization of [`AgentSettings`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/types.ts#L46) and the internal [`_taskState`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L60) into an [`SDKTask`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L7) object, which is then stored. Conversely, the [`reconstruct`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L104) method deserializes this information to restore a task to its previous state. The entire task lifecycle, including state updates and agent activities, is communicated through an [`ExecutionEventBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L34) using [`AgentExecutionEvent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L15) instances, facilitating loose coupling and enabling external components to react to changes.

### CLI Command Management and Execution

link

zoom\_in

The A2A server provides capabilities for defining, registering, and executing command-line interface (CLI) commands, with a focus on integrating these commands into the agentic workflow. This system manages commands for extension management, project initialization, and checkpoint restoration, ensuring their interaction with the agent executor and event bus for streaming updates.

The core of this system is the [`CommandRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/command-registry.ts#L12), implemented in [`packages/a2a-server/src/commands/command-registry.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/command-registry.ts). This registry centrally manages all commands, allowing them to be registered and retrieved by name. It supports both top-level commands and nested subcommands, simplifying the organization of complex CLI functionalities. Commands are defined using a [`Command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/keyBindings.ts#L10) interface, detailed in [`packages/a2a-server/src/commands/types.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/types.ts), which specifies properties like [`name`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/eslint.config.js#L179), [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5), [`arguments`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L17), [`subCommands`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts#L162), and an [`execute`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/ls.ts#L140) method. The [`CommandContext`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/commands/types.ts#L28) provides essential services, such as configuration, a Git service, and an event bus, to commands during their execution.

For **extension management**, the [`ExtensionsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts#L14) and [`ListExtensionsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts#L28) are defined in [`packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts). The [`ExtensionsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts#L14) acts as a top-level entry point, defaulting to listing installed extensions. The [`ListExtensionsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/extensions.ts#L28) specifically retrieves and displays information about installed extensions by utilizing an external utility from the [`@google/gemini-cli-core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/npm.md?plain=1#L17) package.

**Project initialization** is handled by the [`InitCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/init.ts#L25), located in [`packages/a2a-server/src/commands/init.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/init.ts). This command analyzes a project, generates [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) content via an AI agent prompt, and orchestrates the submission of this prompt to the agent executor. It is designed to stream updates via an [`eventBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L116), keeping the client informed of progress. If [`performInit`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/commands/init.ts#L9) requires user input, [`InitCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/init.ts#L25) will submit the prompt to the [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83) for processing, ensuring that the initialization process can be fully automated or interactively guided. See [AI Agent Orchestration and Execution](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ai-agent-orchestration-and-model-management-ai-agent-orchestration-and-execution) for more details on agent execution.

For **checkpoint management**, the system includes [`RestoreCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts#L21) and [`ListCheckpointsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts#L113), both defined in [`packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts). The [`RestoreCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts#L21) enables the restoration of an agent's conversational and file history from a specified JSON checkpoint file. It validates the checkpoint data, calls a core utility to perform the restoration, and handles potential errors. The [`ListCheckpointsCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/restore.ts#L113) provides a way to discover and list all available checkpoints within the project's temporary directory.

All these commands interact with the [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83) ( [`packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts)) for managing agent tasks and leverage an [`ExecutionEventBus`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L34) to publish streaming updates, allowing clients to receive real-time notifications about command execution progress and results. This integration is crucial for responsive and interactive agent-client communication.

### HTTP API and Streaming Interactions

link

zoom\_in

The A2A server exposes an HTTP API to facilitate standardized client-agent communication, enabling real-time updates and tool execution within the Gemini CLI. The API allows clients to interact with the agent for various tasks, including creating new agent tasks, executing CLI commands, retrieving command lists, and accessing task-specific metadata.

The core of the HTTP API functionality is orchestrated by [`createApp`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L151) within [`packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts). This function initializes an Express.js application, configures the necessary task storage (either [`GCSTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L33) for Google Cloud Storage persistence or an [`InMemoryTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L13)), and sets up a [`CoderAgentExecutor`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts#L83) to manage agent task lifecycles.

Key API endpoints include:

- [`POST /tasks`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/endpoints.test.ts#L79): Creates a new agent task, assigning it a [`taskId`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L208) and persisting its initial state.
- [`POST /executeCommand`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.test.ts#L130): Executes specified CLI commands. This endpoint supports streaming updates, where [`TaskStatusUpdateEvent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/agent/task.ts#L36) s are published via an event bus and delivered to the client as Server-Sent Events (SSEs), providing real-time feedback on command progress. Commands requiring a workspace rely on the [`CODER_AGENT_WORKSPACE_PATH`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L104) environment variable.
- [`/listCommands`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L269): Provides a comprehensive list of all available top-level commands, their descriptions, arguments, and any subcommands, by traversing the internal [`commandRegistry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/commands/command-registry.ts#L43).
- [`/tasks/metadata`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/endpoints.test.ts#L140) and [`/tasks/:taskId/metadata`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L304): Allow for retrieval of metadata associated with all tasks or a specific task, respectively.
- [`/.well-known/agent-card.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L346): Supplies descriptive metadata about the agent itself, such as its name and capabilities.

For managing request-specific contexts across asynchronous operations, an [`AsyncLocalStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/promptIdContext.ts#L7) instance named [`requestStorage`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/requestStorage.ts#L10) is utilized. This ensures that data pertinent to a particular HTTP request (e.g., the [`express.Request`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L82) object) remains accessible throughout the request's lifecycle, even through complex asynchronous call stacks, without explicit passing.

The server's entry point is defined in [`packages/a2a-server/src/http/server.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/server.ts), which is responsible for starting the Express server and implementing global error handling for [`uncaughtException`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/telemetry_utils.js#L448) to ensure graceful process termination.

### Task Persistence with Google Cloud Storage

link

zoom\_in

The A2A server employs a persistence mechanism to store and retrieve the state of agent tasks, ensuring that work can be resumed across sessions or in case of interruptions. This functionality is primarily handled within the [`packages/a2a-server/src/persistence`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence) directory, with Google Cloud Storage (GCS) serving as the backend.

The [`GCSTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L33) class is responsible for interacting with GCS. It saves both the task's metadata (e.g., agent settings, current state) and its associated workspace files. Task metadata is serialized to JSON and compressed using [`gzipSync`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L8) before being uploaded to GCS. The workspace, representing the local directory where the agent operates, is archived into a gzipped tarball using [`tar.c`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L129) and then uploaded to GCS. When a task needs to be restored, [`GCSTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L33) retrieves these compressed files from GCS, decompresses the metadata, and extracts the workspace tarball, effectively reconstructing the agent's state and working environment.

A key aspect of this persistence mechanism is its focus on security and robustness. The [`GCSTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L33) validates [`taskId`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L208) values to prevent path traversal vulnerabilities, ensuring that malicious [`taskId`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts#L208) inputs cannot lead to unauthorized file access or manipulation on the storage system. Temporary files generated during the archiving and extraction processes are properly managed and cleaned up to prevent resource leaks.

In scenarios where task saving might be intentionally disabled, a [`NoOpTaskStore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/a2a-server/src/persistence/gcs.ts#L301) is provided. This class allows the system to continue operating without persisting task state, while still supporting the loading of tasks from an existing store if needed. This selective persistence offers flexibility in how agent tasks are managed, particularly in ephemeral or read-only environments. For more information on the A2A server's overall architecture, see [Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Communication Server](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#agent-to-agent-a2a-communication-server).

## Gemini CLI Tooling and Extensions

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI provides a rich set of built-in tools that enable the Gemini model to interact with the local environment, perform actions, and access information beyond basic text generation. These tools allow the model to operate within a user's filesystem, execute shell commands, retrieve web content, manage persistent memory, and facilitate task breakdown.

At its core, the CLI offers several built-in functionalities to empower the Gemini model:

- **File System Interaction** is managed by tools such as [`list_directory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L555), [`read_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84), [`write_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84), [`glob`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts#L83), [`search_file_content`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md?plain=1#L120), and [`replace`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts#L81) as detailed in [`docs/tools/file-system.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md). These enable the model to navigate, read, create, and modify files and directories, often with user confirmation for sensitive operations like writing or replacing content.
- **Shell Command Execution** is handled by the [`run_shell_command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L85) tool, described in [`docs/tools/shell.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md). This tool allows the model to execute arbitrary shell commands, supporting both interactive and non-interactive modes, with configurable restrictions and output processing.
- **Web Interaction** capabilities include [`web_fetch`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-fetch.md?plain=1#L1), which can summarize, compare, or extract information from web pages given a URL within a prompt, as explained in [`docs/tools/web-fetch.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-fetch.md). Additionally, [`google_web_search`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L90), documented in [`docs/tools/web-search.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-search.md), performs web searches via the Gemini API, returning summarized results with citations.
- **Memory Management** is supported by the [`save_memory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/memory.md?plain=1#L1) tool, outlined in [`docs/tools/memory.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/memory.md). This tool allows the model to store "facts" in a user-editable [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) file, which are then loaded as context in subsequent sessions to provide persistent memory.
- **Task Management** is facilitated by the [`write_todos`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/todos.md?plain=1#L1) tool, detailed in [`docs/tools/todos.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/todos.md). This tool allows the Gemini agent to break down complex requests into a list of subtasks, providing transparency into its plan and progress to the user.

Beyond these built-in tools, the Gemini CLI features an **Extensions Framework** which significantly expands its capabilities. This framework allows developers to create, release, and manage custom extensions, as described in [`docs/extensions`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions). Extensions can package prompts, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and custom commands. The [`gemini-extension.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L140) manifest file is central to defining an extension's metadata, MCP server configurations, and contextual information.

**Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers**, explained in [`docs/tools/mcp-server.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md), are a key component of the extension system. They allow the CLI to discover, register, and execute external tools and resources, effectively bridging the Gemini model with local environments or other services. MCP servers handle tool definitions, execution, resource access, and even support OAuth for secure authentication with remote services. The CLI provides commands for managing MCP server configurations, including adding, listing, and removing servers.

The CLI's agentic loop behavior can be further customized through a robust **Hook System**, thoroughly documented in [`docs/hooks`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks). Hooks are scripts that can be injected at various lifecycle events of the agent, enabling interception, modification, and logging of CLI actions without altering the core source code. These scripts communicate via JSON payloads over standard I/O and can be used for purposes such as adding context before model processing, validating and blocking operations, logging tool usage, optimizing tool selection, and integrating advanced features like RAG-based tool filtering and cross-session memory management. The hook system supports various [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48), allowing fine-grained control over when custom logic is executed within the agent's workflow.

The Gemini CLI provides a suite of built-in tools that enable the Gemini model to interact with the local environment, access information, and perform actions beyond text generation. These tools are managed by the core component, which presents their schemas to the Gemini model, executes requested tools, and returns results. This allows the model to ground its responses with real-time or local data, offering capabilities such as file system operations, shell command execution, web interaction, memory management, and task planning. Security considerations, such as user confirmation for sensitive operations and sandboxing, are integrated into the design of these tools.

**File System Tools**
A set of file system interaction tools are available for managing local files and directories within a defined [`rootDirectory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md?plain=1#L8). These tools include:

- [`list_directory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L555): Lists files and subdirectories, supporting [`ignore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/filesearch/ignore.ts#L50) patterns and [`respect_git_ignore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/glob.ts#L79).
- [`read_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84): Reads content from a specified file path, handling various file types including text and base64-encoded binary data.
- [`write_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84): Writes content to a file path, creating or overwriting files, and requires user confirmation with a diff.
- [`glob`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts#L83): Locates files matching a specified pattern, with options for case sensitivity and respecting Git ignore rules.
- [`search_file_content`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md?plain=1#L120): Searches for a pattern (regex) within file contents, leveraging [`git grep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L20) where available.
- [`replace`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts#L81): Replaces text within a file, featuring a multi-stage edit correction mechanism to refine matches and requiring user confirmation with a diff.
More details on these tools can be found in [`docs/tools/file-system.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md).

**Shell Command Tool**
The [`run_shell_command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L85) tool allows the execution of shell commands as subprocesses, enabling interaction with the underlying system, script execution, and command-line operations within the Gemini CLI. It returns detailed execution information, including standard output, standard error, exit code, and any errors. The tool supports starting background processes and can be configured to enable an interactive shell using [`node-pty`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L127). Command execution can be restricted using allowlists ( [`tools.core`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L161)) and blocklists ( [`tools.exclude`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L161)) defined in [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322). For more information, refer to [`docs/tools/shell.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md).

**Web Interaction Tools**
Two primary tools facilitate web interaction:

- [`web_fetch`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-fetch.md?plain=1#L1): Processes web page content from URLs embedded in a [`prompt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/types.ts#L405), enabling summarization, comparison, or extraction of information. It requests confirmation before access and can fall back to local fetching if the Gemini API fails to access a URL. This tool is documented in [`docs/tools/web-fetch.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-fetch.md).
- [`google_web_search`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L90): Performs web searches via Google Search through the Gemini API, returning a summarized response with citations based on the query. Further details are available in [`docs/tools/web-search.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/web-search.md).

**Memory Tool**
The [`save_memory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/memory.md?plain=1#L1) tool allows for the persistence of "facts" across CLI sessions. It stores user-provided facts in a Markdown file, [`~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/gemini-md.md?plain=1#L19), under a dedicated section, which is then loaded as context in subsequent sessions to enhance personalized assistance. More details can be found in [`docs/tools/memory.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/memory.md).

**Task Management Tool**
The [`write_todos`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/todos.md?plain=1#L1) tool enables the Gemini agent to break down complex, multi-step requests into actionable "todo" items. This list is dynamically updated by the agent, providing transparency into its current workflow and future steps. The tool accepts an array of objects, each representing a subtask with a [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5) and [`status`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/retry.ts#L113) ( [`pending`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/types.ts#L48), [`in_progress`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts#L92), [`completed`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts#L94), or [`cancelled`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useGitBranchName.ts#L45)). The currently [`in_progress`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts#L92) task is prominently displayed to the user, and the full todo list can be toggled. For more information, see [`docs/tools/todos.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/todos.md).

**Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Integration**
Beyond these built-in tools, the Gemini CLI extends its capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. These servers allow the CLI to interact with external systems by exposing additional tools and resources. The integration includes a discovery layer ( [`mcp-client.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L31)) that discovers and registers tools from configured servers, and an execution layer ( [`mcp-tool.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L45)) that handles tool execution and response processing. MCP servers can be configured in [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322), support OAuth for secure authentication, and can expose contextual resources and predefined prompts. The [`gemini mcp`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) command provides management capabilities for server configurations. Refer to [`docs/tools/mcp-server.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md) for a comprehensive overview of MCP server integration.

All these tools operate within sandboxing restrictions to mitigate risks, and sensitive operations often require user confirmation, as discussed in [Gemini CLI Application Core](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-application-core).

These tools extend the CLI's capabilities beyond text generation, enabling it to perform actions directly within the user's environment. All operations are conducted within a defined root directory, ensuring that file paths are resolved relative to this specified location. Crucially, these tools incorporate security features such as user confirmation for sensitive actions and sandboxing to mitigate potential risks.

For file system interactions, the [`list_directory`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L555) tool, documented in [`docs/tools/file-system.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md), enables the model to list directory contents, with options for filtering based on [`ignore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/filesearch/ignore.ts#L50) patterns and [`.gitignore`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/settings.md?plain=1#L81) files. To locate files matching specific patterns, the [`glob`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts#L83) tool is used. The [`search_file_content`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md?plain=1#L120) tool performs text searches within file contents, leveraging [`git grep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L20) for efficiency when available. For modifications, the [`write_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84) tool creates or overwrites files and requires user confirmation, presenting a diff of proposed changes before execution. Similarly, the [`replace`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts#L81) tool, also detailed in [`docs/tools/file-system.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/file-system.md), handles in-place string replacements within files. The [`run_shell_command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L85) tool, described in [`docs/tools/shell.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md), provides the capability to execute shell commands as subprocesses. It supports both non-interactive and, when configured, interactive operations, capturing detailed execution information such as standard output, standard error, and exit codes. The behavior of this tool can be configured via [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322) to enable an interactive shell using [`node-pty`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L127) and to control output formatting. ### Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Integration

link

zoom\_in

Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers extend the capabilities of the Gemini CLI by allowing it to interact with external systems and services. These servers act as a bridge, enabling the CLI to discover, register, and execute custom tools and access resources that go beyond its built-in functionalities. This integration facilitates a more dynamic and expansive environment for the Gemini model, allowing it to perform a wider range of actions.

The core functionality of MCP servers encompasses the discovery of available tools, their execution with specified arguments, and the retrieval of structured responses. Additionally, they allow access to contextual resources and support the definition and invocation of predefined prompts as slash commands within the CLI.

The integration architecture is built upon a discovery layer and an execution layer. The discovery layer, primarily managed by the [`discoverMcpTools`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts#L712) function, iterates through configured MCP servers, establishes connections using various transports (Stdio, SSE, or Streamable HTTP), and fetches tool definitions and resources. It then sanitizes and validates these tool schemas to ensure compatibility with the Gemini API and registers them in a global registry. The execution layer wraps each discovered MCP tool, handling confirmation logic based on trust settings, managing the execution of tools by calling the MCP server with prepared parameters, and processing responses for both the LLM context and user display.

MCP server configurations are managed within the [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322) file, allowing for global settings that apply to all MCP servers, as well as server-specific configurations. These configurations include details such as the command to start a server, URLs for HTTP or SSE transports, arguments, HTTP headers, environment variables, and working directories. Critical settings like [`timeout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/add.ts#L34) and [`trust`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/add.ts#L35) also determine the behavior of tool execution and confirmation prompts.

The CLI supports OAuth 2.0 for remote MCP servers, managing token storage and refresh. This enables secure authentication for external services. Furthermore, MCP servers can expose contextual resources, which can be referenced in conversations and read by the CLI to inject content. Predefined prompts from MCP servers can also be invoked as slash commands, offering quick access to server-specific functionalities.

For managing MCP server configurations programmatically, the [`gemini mcp`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) CLI command provides subcommands to add, list, and remove server settings. This allows users to control the integration of external services with the Gemini CLI. The system also tracks the status of MCP servers and their discovery processes, offering mechanisms for troubleshooting common issues related to connectivity, tool discovery, and execution within the sandboxed environment. For more information on command-line tools, see [Built-in Tools for Local Environment Interaction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-built-in-tools-for-local-environment-interaction).

### Gemini CLI Extensions Framework

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI provides an extensions framework to enhance its capabilities, allowing developers to package custom prompts, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and CLI commands. This framework is documented in [`docs/extensions`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions).

Extensions are defined by a [`gemini-extension.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L140) manifest, which specifies metadata such as the extension's [`name`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/eslint.config.js#L179) and [`version`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/get-release-version.js#L110), and configures [`mcpServers`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/policy.ts#L27). These servers facilitate the integration of custom tools that the Gemini model can invoke. The framework supports context provisioning through a [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113) file, allowing developers to provide persistent contextual instructions to the model.

For local development, extensions can be bootstrapped using [`gemini extensions new`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) and symbolically linked with [`gemini extensions link .`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/telemetry.md?plain=1#L483). This enables immediate testing of changes. Custom tools within an extension are typically implemented via an [`McpServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/schema.ts#L87) using the [`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/GEMINI.md?plain=1#L55). The [`McpServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/zed-integration/schema.ts#L87) registers tools with defined [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5) s and [`inputSchema`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts#L77) s (using [`zod`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L848)), which the Gemini CLI interacts with over standard I/O via a [`StdioServerTransport`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L847).

Custom CLI commands can also be defined within an extension using TOML files, specifying prompt templates and shell command interpolations. This allows for creating shortcuts that execute shell commands and feed their output directly into a prompt for model processing.

The framework supports various mechanisms for managing extensions:

- **Installation**: Extensions can be installed from Git repositories or GitHub Releases using [`gemini extensions install`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1), with options to specify [`ref`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/tools.ts#L594) s for version control, enable auto-updates, or install pre-release versions.
- **Uninstallation**: [`gemini extensions uninstall`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L361) removes an extension.
- **Activation Control**: [`gemini extensions enable`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L96) and [`gemini extensions disable`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/settings.md?plain=1#L1) manage whether an extension is active, with support for user or workspace-specific scopes.
- **Updates**: [`gemini extensions update`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/faq.md?plain=1#L48) fetches the latest changes for individual or all installed extensions.
- **Settings Management**: [`gemini extensions settings list`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) and [`gemini extensions settings set`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) allow viewing and modifying extension-specific settings, which can include sensitive data stored securely in a keychain.

When conflicts arise, workspace configurations take precedence over extension configurations. Similarly, if an extension command conflicts with a user or project command, the extension command is prefixed to avoid naming collisions. Changes made via extension management commands generally require a CLI restart to take effect.

For distributing extensions, both Git repository and GitHub Releases are supported. Git repository releases offer flexibility, allowing installation directly from a URI and targeting specific branches, tags, or commits for version control. GitHub Releases, on the other hand, optimize for faster initial installations by shipping extensions as archives, with support for marking releases as "latest" and handling pre-releases. Crucially, for platform-specific binaries, GitHub Release assets follow a specific naming convention ( [`{platform}.{arch}.{name}.{extension}`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md?plain=1#L109)) to enable the CLI to automatically identify and download the correct binary for the user's operating system and architecture. An example GitHub Actions workflow is provided to automate multi-platform releases. See [Extension Development and Configuration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-gemini-cli-extensions-framework-extension-development-and-configuration) and [Extension Release and Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-gemini-cli-extensions-framework-extension-release-and-management) for more details.

#### Extension Development and Configuration
