Extensions for the Gemini CLI enable developers to expand its capabilities by packaging prompts, custom commands, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. The process of bootstrapping a new extension begins with the [`gemini extensions new`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) command, which initializes a project from a predefined template. This command, especially when used with the [`mcp-server`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/GEMINI.md?plain=1#L248) template, sets up the basic structure for an extension that includes a server component. Local development is facilitated by the [`gemini extensions link .`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/telemetry.md?plain=1#L483) command, which symbolically links the current directory as an extension, allowing for immediate testing of changes without needing to reinstall.

The core of an extension's configuration resides in the [`gemini-extension.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L140) manifest file. This file defines crucial metadata such as the extension's [`name`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/eslint.config.js#L179) and [`version`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/get-release-version.js#L110), along with configurations for any [`mcpServers`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/policy.ts#L27). It also allows for specifying a [`contextFileName`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useShowMemoryCommand.ts#L35), typically [`GEMINI.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L113), which provides persistent contextual instructions to the Gemini model. This mechanism ensures that the model can maintain a consistent persona or receive specific guidance on tool usage. Additionally, [`gemini-extension.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L140) supports variable substitution for dynamic paths, such as [`${extensionPath}`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L291) and [`${workspacePath}`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L292), enhancing portability. For further details on extension configuration and management, refer to the [Gemini CLI Extensions Framework](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-gemini-cli-extensions-framework) section.

Custom tools, which allow the Gemini model to interact with external services or perform specific actions, are implemented via an MCP server. This server, often written in TypeScript and leveraging [`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/GEMINI.md?plain=1#L55), defines tools using the [`registerTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/config/config.ts#L1538) method. Each tool definition includes a [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5) and an [`inputSchema`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts#L77) (defined using [`zod`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L848) for type validation) along with an asynchronous function that executes the tool's logic. Communication between the Gemini CLI and the MCP server is typically handled over standard I/O using [`StdioServerTransport`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L847) from [`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L847), enabling the CLI to invoke these custom tools.

Beyond custom tools, extensions can also define custom CLI commands. These commands are specified in TOML files located within a [`commands/`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L244) subdirectory of the extension. Each TOML file defines a [`prompt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/types.ts#L405) template, which can incorporate command-line argument placeholders (e.g., [`{{args}}`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/custom-commands.md?plain=1#L56)) and shell command interpolations. This allows developers to create powerful shortcuts that execute shell commands and feed their output directly into a prompt for model processing. In cases of command name conflicts with user or project commands, extension commands are automatically prefixed (e.g., [`/gcp.deploy`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L278)) to ensure uniqueness.

#### Extension Release and Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI provides robust mechanisms for managing extensions throughout their lifecycle, from installation and updates to activation control and settings management. Extensions can be distributed in two primary ways: via Git repositories or through GitHub Releases.

Extensions can be installed from a Git repository using the [`gemini extensions install <your-repo-uri>`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md?plain=1#L3) command, allowing users to specify a particular Git [`ref`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/tools.ts#L594) (branch, tag, or commit) for version control. This method offers flexibility, enabling developers to manage different release channels (e.g., [`stable`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L71), [`preview`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L61), [`dev`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/start.js#L66)) using branches or tags. For Git-based installations, the [`HEAD`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/lint.js#L204) commit of the specified [`ref`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/tools/tools.ts#L594) is considered the latest version, simplifying continuous updates and rollbacks.

Alternatively, GitHub Releases can be utilized, which often provides faster initial installations, especially for extensions with platform-specific binaries. This method supports marking releases as "latest" and allows for the installation of specific releases using [`--ref=<some-release-tag>`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md?plain=1#L81) or pre-releases with the [`--pre-release`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L45) flag. For extensions that require a build step or include platform-specific binaries, custom archives can be attached to GitHub releases. The CLI relies on a specific naming convention for these archives ( [`{platform}.{arch}.{name}.{extension}`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md?plain=1#L109)) to automatically detect and download the correct asset for the user's operating system and architecture. An example GitHub Actions workflow is provided to automate multi-platform release generation, ensuring that necessary binaries for platforms like Darwin, Linux, and Windows across [`x64`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L129) and [`arm64`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L128) architectures are correctly built and attached. The archive structure requires the [`gemini-extension.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L140) file to be at the root of the archive to ensure consistency and facilitate installation. More details on the release mechanisms can be found in [`docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/extension-releasing.md).

Once installed, extensions can be managed using a suite of commands. The [`gemini extensions uninstall`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L361) command removes an extension. Activation can be controlled with [`gemini extensions disable`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/settings.md?plain=1#L1) and [`gemini extensions enable`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L96), supporting [`--scope`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L924) for user or workspace-specific control. Extensions can be updated individually or all at once using [`gemini extensions update`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/faq.md?plain=1#L48) with the [`--all`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md?plain=1#L98) flag. For development purposes, [`gemini extensions link .`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/cli/telemetry.md?plain=1#L483) creates a symbolic link to the current directory, streamlining local testing of changes.

Extensions also support configurable settings, which can be viewed using [`gemini extensions settings list`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) and updated with [`gemini extensions settings set`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1). These settings are stored in [`.env`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/faq.md?plain=1#L92) files within the extension's directory and can be marked as [`sensitive`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionSettings.ts#L29) to trigger secure keychain storage. It's important to note that most changes made via [`gemini extensions`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L1) commands, such as installation, uninstallation, enabling, or disabling, require a CLI restart to take effect. Further details on extension management and configuration are available in [`docs/extensions/index.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/extensions/index.md). For information on defining extension configurations, refer to [Extension Development and Configuration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-gemini-cli-extensions-framework-extension-development-and-configuration).

### Customizing Agent Behavior with Hooks

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI's hook system enables dynamic customization of the agentic loop by allowing external scripts to intercept, modify, and log CLI actions without altering the core source code. This pluggable architecture facilitates advanced behaviors, policy enforcement, and optimization of agent interactions. The system supports various [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48) that trigger custom scripts at specific points in the CLI's lifecycle, managing their execution and output to influence the CLI's behavior. The documentation within [`docs/hooks`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks) provides comprehensive guidance on leveraging this system.

Hooks operate synchronously, pausing the CLI's agent loop until all relevant scripts complete. Communication between the CLI and hooks is facilitated through JSON payloads exchanged via standard input and output. The exit code of a command hook determines its impact: a [`0`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/LICENSE#L3) indicates success, [`2`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/LICENSE#L3) signifies a blocking error, and any other code results in a non-blocking warning.

Key functionalities enabled by the hook system include:

- **Context Addition:** Scripts can inject additional information before the model processes a prompt, enriching the agent's understanding.
- **Validation and Blocking:** Hooks can review and, if necessary, block operations that are deemed dangerous or non-compliant, providing a mechanism for policy enforcement. For example, the [`security.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md?plain=1#L387) script discussed in [`docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md) demonstrates how to intercept [`write_file`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L84) or [`replace`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/utils/llm-edit-fixer.ts#L81) operations to prevent sensitive data from being exposed.
- **Logging and Monitoring:** The system allows for detailed logging of tool usage and model responses, which can be crucial for auditing and debugging.
- **Optimization:** Hooks can dynamically adjust tool selection or modify model parameters, potentially leading to improved performance and cost efficiency. The [`rag-filter.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md?plain=1#L374) script described in [`docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md) illustrates how a fast LLM can be used to filter available tools based on user input, optimizing tool selection for better accuracy and cost.

The system supports various [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48), such as [`SessionStart`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1527) for initialization, [`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491) for pre-planning context additions, [`BeforeTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1467) for argument validation, and [`AfterTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1479) for post-execution processing. Hooks are defined in [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322) files, allowing for granular control and configurable execution based on [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) patterns. These matchers support exact matches, regular expressions, and wildcards, enabling precise targeting of events or tools. The [`/hooks panel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L451) command provides a view of all registered hooks and their status. Further details on hook events and execution flow are available in [Hook Event Types and Execution Flow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-customizing-agent-behavior-with-hooks-hook-event-types-and-execution-flow).

Best practices for developing and managing hooks emphasize security, performance, debugging, and privacy. This includes input validation, setting timeouts, limiting permissions, optimizing script execution, and carefully managing telemetry data. Detailed guidance on these aspects is provided in [`docs/hooks/best-practices.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/best-practices.md). For practical examples of creating and configuring hooks, including advanced scenarios like cross-session memory management, refer to [`docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/writing-hooks.md).

#### Hook Event Types and Execution Flow

link

| Hook Event / Config Property | Description |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Hook Events** |  |
| `SessionStart` | Initializes resources or loads context when a session begins. |
| `SessionEnd` | Cleans up resources or saves state when a session ends. |
| `BeforeAgent` | Adds context or validates prompts after user input but before agent planning. |
| `AfterAgent` | Reviews output or forces continuation when the agent loop concludes. |
| `BeforeModel` | Modifies prompts or adds instructions before sending a request to the LLM. |
| `AfterModel` | Filters responses or logs interactions after receiving a response from the LLM. |
| `BeforeToolSelection` | Filters available tools or optimizes selection before the LLM chooses tools. |
| `BeforeTool` | Validates arguments or blocks dangerous operations before a tool executes. |
| `AfterTool` | Processes results or runs tests after a tool has executed. |
| `PreCompress` | Saves state or notifies the user before context compression occurs. |
| `Notification` | Auto-approves or logs decisions when a notification (e.g., permission) fires. |
| **Hook Configuration Properties** |  |
| `name` | Unique identifier for managing the hook. |
| `type` | Specifies the hook type; currently, only `"command"` is supported. |
| `command` | Path to the script or command the hook executes. |
| `description` | Human-readable explanation of the hook's purpose. |
| `timeout` | Maximum execution time for the hook in milliseconds. |
| `matcher` | Pattern to filter when the hook runs, applicable to tool-related and some event-specific hooks. |

The Gemini CLI integrates a hook system to enable dynamic customization and extension of its agentic loop. This system allows scripts to be injected at various predefined [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48) in the CLI's lifecycle, providing opportunities to intercept, modify, and log actions without altering the application's core source code. Hooks execute synchronously, pausing the CLI's agent loop until their completion. Communication between the CLI and the hooks occurs via JSON payloads transmitted over standard input and output.

Key [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48) and their triggers include:

- **[`SessionStart`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1527)**: Triggered at the beginning of a CLI session for resource initialization or context loading.
- **[`SessionEnd`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1539)**: Occurs at the conclusion of a session, enabling cleanup operations or state saving.
- **[`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491)**: Fires after a user prompt but before the AI agent begins its planning phase, allowing for additional context injection or prompt validation.
- **[`AfterAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1503)**: Executes once the agentic loop has completed, providing an opportunity for reviewing output or forcing continued execution.
- **[`BeforeModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1563)**: Triggered before a request is sent to the Large Language Model (LLM), facilitating prompt modification or instruction injection.
- **[`AfterModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1575)**: Occurs after receiving a response from the LLM, enabling filtering or logging of the model's output.
- **[`BeforeToolSelection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1587)**: Initiated before the LLM selects tools to use, allowing for filtering of available tools or optimization of the selection process.
- **[`BeforeTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1467)**: Fires just before a tool is executed, providing a point for argument validation or blocking potentially sensitive operations.
- **[`AfterTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1479)**: Triggered after a tool has completed its execution, useful for processing results or integrating automated tests.
- **[`PreCompress`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1551)**: Executes before the context window is compressed, which can be used for saving intermediate states or notifying users.
- **[`Notification`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1515)**: Occurs when a notification event happens, such as a permission request, allowing for automated approvals or logging of decisions.

Hooks are configured in [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322) files, with specific properties including a [`name`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/eslint.config.js#L179), [`type`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/deflake.js#L56) (currently [`"command"`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L365), indicating execution of a shell command or script), the [`command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L365) path, an optional [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5), a [`timeout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/add.ts#L34) in milliseconds, and a [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) pattern. The [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) property allows for fine-grained control over which tools or event sources trigger a hook, supporting exact matches, regular expressions, and wildcards. The execution order of hooks is determined by their declaration within each configuration layer, with precedence given to user, project, and system settings. Within a hook script, environment variables like [`GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookRunner.ts#L209), [`GEMINI_SESSION_ID`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L466), and [`GEMINI_API_KEY`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L173) are accessible, providing contextual information for script execution.

The synchronous nature of hook execution means that prompt scripts should be optimized for performance to avoid negatively impacting the CLI's responsiveness. Hooks indicate their outcome using standard Unix exit codes: [`0`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/LICENSE#L3) for success, [`2`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/LICENSE#L3) for a blocking error, and other codes for non-blocking warnings. This contract ensures that the CLI can react appropriately to hook outcomes, such as displaying error messages to the user or preventing an operation from proceeding. For further details on developing and managing hooks, including best practices for security, performance, and debugging, refer to [Developing and Managing Hooks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-customizing-agent-behavior-with-hooks-developing-and-managing-hooks) and [Customizing Agent Behavior with Hooks](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-customizing-agent-behavior-with-hooks).

#### Developing and Managing Hooks

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI's hook system allows for significant customization of the agentic loop through the injection of external scripts. These scripts, written in languages such as Bash or Node.js, interact with the CLI by receiving JSON input on standard input (stdin) and providing JSON output on standard output (stdout), influencing the CLI's behavior. This mechanism enables advanced functionalities like logging tool executions, preventing sensitive data from being written, automating tests, and dynamically injecting context into agent interactions.

Hooks are configured within the [`settings.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/README.md?plain=1#L322) files, where each hook definition includes a [`name`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/eslint.config.js#L179), [`type`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/deflake.js#L56) (currently limited to [`"command"`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L365)), and the [`command`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L365) path to the executable script. Optional properties such as a [`description`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/shell.md?plain=1#L5), [`timeout`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/commands/mcp/add.ts#L34), and a [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) pattern allow for fine-grained control over hook behavior and execution. The [`matcher`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.ts#L79) is particularly useful for filtering which tools or event sources trigger a hook, supporting exact matches, regular expressions, and wildcards.

The system supports various [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48) that trigger custom scripts at specific points in the agent's lifecycle. For instance, a [`BeforeTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1467) hook can validate arguments or block sensitive operations before a tool executes, while an [`AfterTool`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1479) hook can process results or trigger automated tests. The [`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491) hook can inject additional context, such as recent Git commits, before the agent plans its actions.

Advanced applications include RAG-based tool filtering, where a [`BeforeToolSelection`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1587) hook can leverage a fast Large Language Model (LLM) to extract keywords from user input and dynamically filter the set of available tools, optimizing accuracy and cost. Another example is cross-session memory management, achieved through a suite of hooks triggered at [`SessionStart`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1527), [`BeforeAgent`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1491), [`AfterModel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1575), and [`SessionEnd`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L1539). These hooks collectively initialize a vector database, retrieve relevant memories based on the current prompt, record user interactions, and consolidate learnings for persistent storage.

Best practices for developing hooks emphasize security, performance, debugging, and privacy. Security considerations include input validation, setting timeouts, limiting permissions, and sandboxing untrusted hooks. For performance, hooks should be designed for fast execution, with caching mechanisms and appropriate [`Hook Events`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx#L48) selection to avoid unnecessary processing. Debugging can be aided by logging to files, using standard error (stderr), and utilizing the [`/hooks panel`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/hooks/index.md?plain=1#L451) command, which provides a view of registered hooks and their execution status. Privacy considerations involve careful management of [`telemetry`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/integration-tests/test-helper.ts#L312) data collection and sensitive information within hooks, with recommendations for minimizing logging and sanitizing outputs. For more details on hook events and their execution flow, refer to [Hook Event Types and Execution Flow](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#gemini-cli-tooling-and-extensions-customizing-agent-behavior-with-hooks-hook-event-types-and-execution-flow).

## IDE Integration

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI offers integration with Integrated Development Environments (IDEs), primarily through a dedicated VS Code extension, to enhance the developer experience by providing contextual awareness and interactive features. This integration allows the CLI to access information from the user's active IDE session and present AI-generated content, such as code modifications, directly within the IDE's native UI.

The core functionalities of the IDE integration include:

- **Editor Context**: The Gemini CLI can gather information about the user's workspace, including recently accessed files, active cursor positions, and selected text. This context helps the Gemini models understand the user's current focus and tailor their responses more effectively. The [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts) module, for instance, actively monitors open files and selection changes to maintain an up-to-date [`IdeContext`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/cli/src/ui/AppContainer.tsx#L35).
- **Native Diffing**: When the Gemini CLI proposes code changes, these modifications can be displayed directly within the IDE's built-in diff viewer. Users can then review, edit, accept, or reject these changes using familiar IDE interactions. The [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) in [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts) is responsible for orchestrating these diff views and handling user feedback.
- **CLI Launch from IDE**: A dedicated command within the IDE's Command Palette ( [`Gemini CLI: Run`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L7)) allows users to quickly launch a new Gemini CLI session, streamlining the workflow between the IDE and the CLI.

The integration is facilitated by the [`Gemini CLI Companion`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L217) VS Code extension, located in [`packages/vscode-ide-companion`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion). This extension acts as a bridge, establishing communication between the IDE and the CLI. It uses an [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts)) to manage an HTTP server that exposes endpoints for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling structured communication. The specification for these IDE companion plugins is detailed in [`docs/ide-integration/ide-companion-spec.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/ide-integration/ide-companion-spec.md).

Installation and management of the IDE integration can occur through various methods, including automatic prompts, manual installation via the CLI ( [`/ide install`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/index.md?plain=1#L38)), or directly from marketplace extensions. The system also includes considerations for sandboxed environments, such as Docker containers, to ensure connectivity between the CLI and the IDE. Troubleshooting guides in [`docs/ide-integration/index.md`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/ide-integration/index.md) address common connection and configuration issues.

Utilities for development and release of the VS Code extension are provided in [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts). These scripts automate tasks such as checking for new releases ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts/check-vscode-release.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts/check-vscode-release.js)) and generating [`NOTICES.txt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/.vscodeignore#L6) files for dependency license compliance ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts/generate-notices.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts/generate-notices.js)). The extension's build process is configured using [`esbuild`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/esbuild.config.js#L13) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/esbuild.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/esbuild.js)) to handle both production and development builds.

### VS Code Extension Architecture

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI VS Code extension ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion)) integrates the Gemini CLI with the VS Code environment, providing contextual information from the IDE to the CLI. This enables the CLI to understand open files, cursor positions, and selected text, and allows proposed code changes to be viewed and managed natively within VS Code. The extension also includes a command to launch the Gemini CLI directly from the IDE.

The extension's lifecycle is managed by its [`activate`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts#L106) and [`deactivate`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts#L219) functions, which serve as its entry and exit points. Upon activation, the extension initializes an [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) to handle communication with the Gemini CLI. It also sets up components for diff management, registers VS Code commands, and performs checks for extension updates. The [`deactivate`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts#L219) function is responsible for gracefully shutting down the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) and disposing of other resources.

A central component of this architecture is the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts)), which establishes an HTTP server for secure communication between the VS Code extension and the Gemini CLI. This server implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP), exposing endpoints that allow the CLI to interact with the IDE. It handles authentication using bearer tokens, enforces CORS policies, and validates host headers to ensure secure communication. The [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) also broadcasts updates about the IDE's context, such as open files and diff statuses, to connected MCP clients.

IDE context, including active files, cursor position, and selected text, is managed by the [`OpenFilesManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts#L19) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts)). This component listens for various VS Code events—such as changes to the active text editor, text selections, document closures, and file deletions or renames—to maintain an up-to-date representation of the IDE's state. It ensures that this contextual information is available to the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) for broadcasting to the CLI.

For managing proposed code changes, the [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts)) and [`DiffContentProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L16) are used. The [`DiffContentProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L16) supplies dynamic textual content for URIs using a custom [`DIFF_SCHEME`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/extension.ts#L20), allowing VS Code to display temporary diff content without saving it to disk. The [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) orchestrates the creation, display, and management of diff views, enabling users to accept or cancel suggested code changes directly within the VS Code interface. These diff management capabilities are integrated with the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) to allow the CLI to propose and interact with code modifications.

The extension also includes mechanisms for checking and prompting users for updates, ensuring that the extension remains current. Furthermore, utility scripts ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/scripts)) are provided for development and release processes, including automated checks for new releases and the generation of [`NOTICES.txt`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/.vscodeignore#L6) for dependency license compliance. See [Development and Release Utilities](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ide-integration-development-and-release-utilities) for more details.

#### IDE Server and Communication Protocol

link

zoom\_in

The [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) facilitates secure HTTP communication between the VS Code extension and the Gemini CLI using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It handles the server's lifecycle, from starting and stopping to managing environment variables and ensuring authenticated communication. This server binds to [`127.0.0.1`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/ide/ide-client.ts#L675) on a dynamically assigned port to handle requests.

Security is a primary concern for the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115). It enforces a bearer token authentication mechanism, validating requests with a valid [`Authorization: Bearer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/tools/mcp-server.md?plain=1#L430) token and rejecting those without it or with invalid tokens. Additionally, it prevents cross-site request forgery (CSRF) by rejecting HTTP requests containing an [`Origin`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.test.ts#L486) header and ensures host-header injection protection by validating the [`Host`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/development.md?plain=1#L19) header. The server also restricts Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) to allow only non-browser requests, as detailed in [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts).

The [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115) plays a crucial role in providing IDE context to the Gemini CLI. It monitors open files and broadcasts updates about the IDE's state to connected MCP clients, utilizing the [`IdeContextNotificationSchema`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/core/src/ide/types.ts#L69). This ensures the CLI has real-time information about the user's workspace, including recently accessed files, active cursor position, and selected text, as further described in [Context and Diff Management](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ide-integration-vs-code-extension-architecture-context-and-diff-management).

#### Context and Diff Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI integrates with IDEs like VS Code to provide real-time context about the user's workspace and to enable native diffing for proposed code changes. This integration enhances the AI agent's ability to understand the user's environment and allows for a more seamless workflow when modifying files.

The core of this context provision is handled by the [`OpenFilesManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts#L19) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts)). This component monitors various VS Code events to keep track of currently open files, the active cursor position, and any selected text. When a user opens a new file, switches tabs, moves their cursor, or selects text, the [`OpenFilesManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/open-files-manager.ts#L19) updates its internal state. This state, which includes information about the 10 most recently accessed files, the active file's cursor position, and up to 16KB of selected text, is then provided to the Gemini CLI. This allows the AI to consider the user's immediate focus when generating responses or suggesting actions.

For managing proposed code changes, the [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) ( [`packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts)) facilitates native diffing within the IDE. When the Gemini CLI suggests modifications to a file, the [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) is responsible for creating and displaying a diff view directly in VS Code. This allows users to review the proposed changes, compare them with the original content, and either accept or reject them using familiar IDE interactions. The [`DiffContentProvider`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L16) within the [`DiffManager`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/diff-manager.ts#L52) dynamically supplies the content for these diff views, ensuring that proposed changes are shown without being saved to disk prematurely. User actions on these diffs, such as acceptance or rejection, are communicated back to the Gemini CLI, allowing the AI to understand the outcome of its suggestions. The communication between the IDE extension and the Gemini CLI is facilitated by the [`IDEServer`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/ide-server.ts#L115). For more details on the communication protocol, refer to [IDE Server and Communication Protocol](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ide-integration-vs-code-extension-architecture-ide-server-and-communication-protocol).

The overall goal of these components is to bridge the gap between the terminal-based Gemini CLI and the graphical IDE, providing a richer and more integrated development experience. The [IDE Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#ide-integration) section provides further details on the capabilities and setup of this integration.

Local workspace packages and the root package are excluded from this validation, as their integrity is managed differently within the monorepo structure.

To prevent running the application with outdated builds, a build status verification mechanism is in place. The [`scripts/check-build-status.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/check-build-status.js) script compares the modification times of source files against the last build timestamp. If any source file is newer than the build timestamp, it indicates an outdated build. Instead of failing outright, this check generates warnings that are communicated to the user, prompting a rebuild. This design allows the application to launch while still informing the developer of potential issues, promoting a smoother development experience.

Finally, pre-commit hooks are integrated into the development workflow to apply these quality checks automatically before code is committed. The [`scripts/pre-commit.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/pre-commit.js) script leverages [`lint-staged`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L106) to execute linters only on the files staged for commit. This ensures that only high-quality code enters the version control system, catching issues proactively rather than reactively in later stages of the CI/CD pipeline. This early detection helps maintain a clean and reliable codebase by making code quality a built-in part of the developer's commit process.

### Sandboxed Environment Management

link

zoom\_in

The Gemini CLI application utilizes sandboxed environments to execute commands securely, primarily using Docker or Podman. This approach isolates the CLI's operations from the host system, enhancing security and ensuring consistent execution across different environments. The management of these sandboxed environments involves building the necessary container images, dynamically determining the appropriate sandboxing tool available on the host system, and integrating this mechanism into the application's startup process.

The process of building a sandboxed environment image for the Gemini CLI is automated by the script located at [`scripts/build_sandbox.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/build_sandbox.js). This script packs the core CLI packages into [`.tgz`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L47) files and then uses a containerization tool (Docker or Podman) to build an image that includes these packages. This ensures that the sandboxed environment has all the necessary dependencies to run the Gemini CLI. The script allows for customization, such as specifying a custom Dockerfile or image name, and includes logic to detect the sandbox command (e.g., [`docker`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/releases.md?plain=1#L363), [`podman`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L45)).

During the application's startup, the [`start.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L20) script, located at [`scripts/start.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/start.js), plays a crucial role in integrating the sandboxing mechanism. It first determines the most suitable sandboxing command available on the system by executing [`scripts/sandbox_command.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/sandbox_command.js). This script checks for the presence of [`docker`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/releases.md?plain=1#L363), [`podman`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L45), or [`sandbox-exec`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L399), prioritizing based on configuration and availability. Once the command is identified, [`start.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/package.json#L20) then launches the main CLI process, potentially within the determined sandboxed environment. This ensures that if sandboxing is enabled, the CLI operates within the isolated container.

The overall automation of the build process, including the sandboxed environment, is orchestrated by [`scripts/build.js`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/build.js), which ensures that dependencies are installed and all packages, including the sandbox image, are built. For more details on the automated build processes, refer to [Monorepo Build and Project Setup Automation](https://codewiki.google/github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli#development-and-release-automation-monorepo-build-and-project-setup-automation).

### Release Management and Patch Automation

link

zoom\_in

The project automates its release processes, encompassing the calculation of version numbers, preparation of GitHub releases, and the execution of a workflow for creating, triggering, and commenting on patch release pull requests.

The process of calculating and retrieving release version information for different release channels (nightly, stable, preview, and patch) is handled by scripts that interact with Git, npm, and GitHub to manage versioning and detect potential conflicts.

For preparing GitHub releases, a dedicated script copies necessary assets, updates package configurations, and modifies [`package.json`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/docs/faq.md?plain=1#L27) files for various packages within the monorepo. This ensures that the packages are correctly configured and bundled for distribution.

A specialized set of scripts manages the intricate patch release workflow. One script creates a patch release Pull Request (PR) by performing Git operations such as cherry-picking commits, creating new branches, and then using the GitHub CLI to open the PR. Another script initiates the patch release workflow by triggering a GitHub Actions workflow, passing relevant details as inputs, and subsequently posting a formatted comment to the original PR to track progress. Finally, other scripts manage commenting on GitHub PRs after the patch creation process, analyzing logs to identify issues (e.g., permissions, existing PRs) and constructing detailed Markdown comments with status updates, links to PRs or workflow runs, and instructions for next steps. This ensures clear communication and tracking throughout the patch release lifecycle.

The management of [`ripgrep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L23) within the application ensures that the correct version is downloaded, extracted, and made available based on the operating system and architecture of the user's environment.

Once identified, the system attempts to download the archive from its source. To optimize performance and reduce redundant downloads, a caching mechanism is in place. If a previously downloaded archive of the specific [`ripgrep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L23) version exists in the cache, it is reused. Otherwise, the archive is downloaded.

After a successful download or cache retrieval, the [`ripgrep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L23) archive is extracted. The extraction method varies depending on the archive type: [`.zip`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/telemetry_utils.js#L218) files are handled specifically, while [`.tar.gz`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/lint.js#L81) archives typically leverage the system's [`tar`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/lint.js#L81) utility. This ensures that the executable [`ripgrep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L23) binary is placed in a designated location where the CLI application can access it. Finally, the system provides the absolute file system path to this [`ripgrep`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/Dockerfile#L23) executable, making it ready for use by other parts of the application. This path is adapted for different operating systems; for instance, it accounts for the [`.exe`](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/cc52839f19798ac0b8b6ea0bc4e25282d390478e/scripts/telemetry_utils.js#L285) extension on Windows platforms.
